ke.headline: Ex-Chief Officer Charged Over Sh1.5 Million Earned Using Forged Certificates
ke.dek: A former Machakos County official faces charges for allegedly using fake academic credentials to secure a senior position and earn over Sh1.5 million.
paragraphs: A former Machakos County chief officer has been charged with fraud after allegedly using forged academic certificates to obtain a senior government position. The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) stated the official earned Sh1,585,967.90 in public funds during his tenure from January to November 2023. He pleaded not guilty to charges including fraudulent acquisition of public property, uttering a false document, and forgery of academic certificates at the Machakos Law Courts.

The EACC investigation revealed the former Chief Officer for Industry and Innovation presented a fraudulent Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Nairobi, purportedly issued in 2004, and a fake Certified Public Accountants (CPA) Final Examination Certificate dated June 2019. These documents were used to secure his appointment. The Director of Public Prosecutions approved the charges following the EACC's inquiry.

The accused was granted cash bail of Sh1 million or an alternative bond of Sh2 million with a surety. The EACC plans to initiate separate civil proceedings to recover the salaries and benefits acquired through the alleged fraudulent qualifications. This case is part of an ongoing EACC crackdown on forged academic papers used by public officials to gain employment.

ke.headline: NCIC Summons Governor Lenku Over Ethnic Remarks
ke.dek: Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku faces arrest if he fails to appear before the National Cohesion and Integration Commission on September 17.
paragraphs: The National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC) has summoned Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku to appear on September 17, 2026, regarding remarks made on August 22. The commission is investigating allegations that Lenku advocated for Maasai candidates to hold political positions in Kajiado and Narok, warning parties against nominating non-Maasai individuals for what he described as Maasai-reserved seats. Failure to appear could result in an arrest warrant and potential criminal or contempt proceedings.

The investigation centers on comments where Lenku reportedly stated, "Any political party that fields a non-Maasai candidate for a position meant for the Maasai in Kajiado, Narok or elsewhere, we will have no relationship with you." He also cited nominations for women’s assembly seats, arguing that only Maasai candidates should be nominated for positions he considered reserved for the community. The NCIC is examining these remarks under provisions of the National Cohesion and Integration Act relating to hate speech and negative ethnicity.

The NCIC, whose mandate includes promoting national unity and guarding against negative ethnicity and hate speech, has not yet made a finding that Governor Lenku has committed an offense. The summons directs Lenku to appear at Britam Towers in Upper Hill, Nairobi, at 2 p.m. on Thursday, September 17, to assist with the ongoing investigation into conduct capable of undermining peaceful relations among communities.

za.headline: Mosimane faces McCarthy in crucial AFCON qualifiers
za.dek: South Africa's new coach Pitso Mosimane will meet Kenya's Benni McCarthy twice in November during the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign.
paragraphs: Pitso Mosimane has been officially appointed as the new head coach of South Africa's men's national football team, Bafana Bafana. This marks Mosimane's second permanent stint in charge, succeeding Hugo Broos. His initial competitive matches are scheduled for September against Guinea and Eritrea. However, the November international window presents a significant challenge as South Africa prepares to host Kenya on November 11 and then travel to face them four days later.

These upcoming fixtures against Kenya, led by fellow South African football icon Benni McCarthy, are particularly critical. Kenya, as co-hosts of the 2027 AFCON, automatically qualify for the tournament. This means only one other team from their qualification group will secure a spot at the continental finals, placing immense pressure on Bafana Bafana to secure positive results.

Mosimane, a highly decorated coach with numerous honours from his time with Mamelodi Sundowns and Al Ahly, now faces a crucial test early in his tenure. The double-header against McCarthy's Kenyan side represents a pivotal moment in the qualification campaign, with dropping points potentially having severe consequences for South Africa's chances of reaching the 2027 AFCON.

za.headline: South African Schools Close for 12-Day Holiday
za.dek: Learners will break for the September holidays after the shortest school term of the year, returning in October.
paragraphs: The third school term in South Africa concludes on Wednesday, September 23, granting students a 12-day break that includes the Heritage Day public holiday. This term, comprising 46 school days, is one of the shortest of the year. Students will resume classes for the fourth term on Tuesday, October 6.

The Department of Basic Education structures the academic year with four terms, aiming to maintain a consistent framework for teaching and learning. The 2026 school year began on January 14 and will conclude on December 9, encompassing a total of 199 school days and 28 school holidays, in addition to six public holidays.

This break comes as matriculants prepare for their mock matric exams, a crucial part of their preparation for final assessments. The academic calendar is reviewed annually to ensure no loss of teaching and learning days, providing a predictable schedule for students and educators nationwide.

za.headline: Public Health Congress Confronts Climate Crisis Impacts
za.dek: Delegates meeting in Cape Town will connect health crises to energy justice and a transition away from fossil fuels.
paragraphs: The 18th World Congress on Public Health convenes in Cape Town this September, offering a platform for global health professionals to address the escalating health impacts of the climate crisis. The congress aims to guide Africa's pursuit of energy justice and a just transition away from fossil fuels, linking various crises from conflict to extreme weather. Attendees will share expertise on illnesses linked to unsafe work, poverty, pollution, and political neglect, all exacerbated by conditions like the super El Niño.

The congress's theme, 'Health Without Borders: Equity, Inclusion, and Sustainability,' calls for understanding and connecting crises often viewed in isolation. The ongoing conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, impacting global oil supplies, serves as a stark example of how fossil fuel dependence creates widespread public health emergencies. Rising oil prices, increased transport and food costs, and fiscal strain on importing nations further pressure already strained health systems.

This gathering provides a crucial opportunity for the public health community to identify shared systems driving ill health, including conflict, energy insecurity, rising costs, pollution, climate change, and inequality. Public health's role extends beyond direct disease causes to examining underlying political, commercial, social, and environmental factors that determine access to essential resources and influence overall well-being.

za.headline: Madlanga Commission Demands Medical Proof for Khan Testimony Delays
za.dek: The commission will not postpone suspended officer Feroz Khan's testimony further without independent medical verification of his inability to appear.
paragraphs: The Madlanga Commission has set a deadline of September 28 for suspended Crime Intelligence officer Major General Feroz Khan to testify, making any further delays conditional on an independent medical assessment. Khan's testimony has been repeatedly postponed due to medical excuses, most recently a hospital admission over the weekend. His legal representative argued against an independent assessment, fearing it could worsen his client's condition.

Commission chair Justice Madlanga ruled that while Khan's medical condition details remain private, his ability to testify must be independently verified. This decision follows scrutiny over altered and backdated sick notes. Khan was injured in a shooting on June 28, shortly before a previous scheduled appearance.

The commission will not force Khan to undergo a medical examination, adopting an approach similar to a previous case. Khan's ongoing medical issues are the latest development in an inquiry where his name has frequently surfaced, including scrutiny of his relationship with former Investigating Directorate Against Corruption head Andrea Johnson.

za.headline: Messi Retires From International Football
za.dek: The 39-year-old Argentina captain announced his retirement on August 31, 2026, after a career spanning 207 caps and 125 goals.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi, 39, has announced his retirement from international football on August 31, 2026, ending a career that included 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina. The decision follows Argentina's runner-up finish at the 2026 World Cup and comes amid personal grief from the recent death of his father, Jorge Messi.

Messi's international journey began in 2005, marked by near-misses in major finals before finally securing the World Cup in 2022, alongside two Copa América titles and the Finalissima. His career was also defined by overcoming a childhood growth hormone deficiency, with his treatment funded by Barcelona.

The legendary forward's departure marks the end of an era for the Argentina national team, leaving a significant void. While his international career concludes, Messi, who plays for Inter Miami CF, will continue his club career through the 2028 season.

ng.headline: Opposition suit against Tinubu's eligibility stalls over service
ng.dek: A legal challenge to President Bola Tinubu's eligibility for the 2027 presidential election has been postponed due to issues with serving the president.
paragraphs: A legal challenge filed by Atiku Abubakar against President Bola Tinubu's eligibility for the 2027 presidential election has been stalled. The court adjourned the case to a new date following a disagreement between lawyers regarding the proper service of the suit on President Tinubu. This development means the legal question of Tinubu's eligibility remains unresolved for now.

The opposition's attempt to unite against President Tinubu for the 2027 election is seen by some as a recurring tactic in Nigerian political history, with past efforts failing against incumbents. Unlike the 2015 election, where a strong opposition coalition formed and made significant sacrifices, the current opposition landscape is described as far from that level of unity and preparedness.

The ruling party, under President Tinubu, currently controls a substantial number of states and possesses a formidable nationwide structure, including a large representation in the National Assembly. This contrasts with the situation in 2015, when the ruling party was fractured and faced significant challenges, including internal defections and external pressures, which paved the way for the opposition's victory.

ng.headline: Driver's Fatigue Causes Fatal Crash, Leads to Six-Year Sentence
ng.dek: A Nigerian-British taxi driver, who drove for nearly three days straight, fell asleep at the wheel and killed a man in the UK.
paragraphs: Kolawole Erunkulu, a taxi driver with joint British and Nigerian nationality, has been sentenced to six years in prison for causing the death of 59-year-old Philip Dray. The fatal collision occurred when Erunkulu, who had been driving for approximately 53 hours with minimal rest, experienced a microsleep. His Audi veered into a layby, striking Mr. Dray as he was about to re-enter his parked Volkswagen. Mr. Dray died at the scene.

Surrey Police revealed that Erunkulu's longest rest period in the three days prior to the crash was only seven hours. In the 12 hours immediately preceding the incident, he had been working as a taxi driver with only short breaks. CCTV footage from inside his vehicle showed Erunkulu nodding off before the car drifted into the layby. He continued driving for about ten seconds after the impact before stopping.

Erunkulu pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving and was sentenced at Guildford Crown Court. He received an eight-year driving ban. The judge noted that Erunkulu was clearly extremely tired and should have stopped driving. Police highlighted the case as an example of the severe dangers associated with driving while fatigued, especially during the early morning hours.

ng.headline: Nigeria's Forex Liquidity Strengthens Amidst Record Diaspora Inflows
ng.dek: External reserves surpass $53 billion as July diaspora remittances reach $947 million, nearing the central bank's target.
paragraphs: Nigeria is experiencing improved foreign exchange liquidity as September begins, with external reserves now exceeding $53 billion. July saw record formal diaspora inflows totaling $947 million, falling just $53 million short of the Central Bank of Nigeria's (CBN) monthly goal of $1 billion. This strengthening liquidity is occurring as Nigeria anticipates a return to the FTSE Russell Frontier Market universe this month.

The naira traded at varying rates across official and parallel markets on September 2, 2026. The official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) recorded the naira at N1,329.43 to the US dollar on September 1, with a closing rate of N1,329.00 per dollar. This official rate is derived from the volume-weighted average of transactions within the formal banking system.

In contrast, the parallel market continued to trade the dollar at higher rates. Aboki Forex reported dollar buying at approximately N1,400 and selling at N1,405 on September 2, while NairaToday placed the rate around N1,410. This disparity highlights the ongoing gap between regulated transactions and rates determined by supply and demand in the informal sector, with actual rates varying by dealer, location, and transaction size.

et.headline: EPSS Wins Gold Award for Supply Chain Excellence
et.dek: The Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Service received a top honor for its reforms in medicine procurement and supply chain management.
paragraphs: The Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Service (EPSS) has been awarded the Gold Award at the fifth Africa Supply Chain Excellence Awards in Pretoria, South Africa. Director General Dr. Abdulkedir Gelgelo stated the award recognizes EPSS's improved performance in pharmaceutical and medical supply procurement and its broader supply-chain management reforms. Digital transformation, enterprise resource planning, and data-driven decision-making were cited as key factors in achieving this recognition, moving EPSS closer to its 2030 vision of becoming a leading African supply-chain institution.

This award highlights EPSS's commitment to quality and encourages pooled procurement for medicines. The state-owned enterprise is responsible for supplying essential medicines to over 420 hospitals, 4,100 health centers, and 18,500 health posts nationwide. Historically, EPSS faced challenges including lengthy procurement cycles that could take up to 400 days, fragmented records, and outdated manual tracking, which limited inventory visibility and disrupted medicine supply.

EPSS has undergone significant public-sector transformation, addressing systemic and operational weaknesses that previously impacted health service delivery. Reforms have focused on legislative changes and digitization to overcome administrative bottlenecks and information shortages. These efforts aim to ensure a more stable, accessible, and reliable supply of pharmaceuticals and medical equipment across the country, improving the efficiency of warehousing and last-mile delivery networks.

et.headline: Deloitte Gains Investment Bank License in Ethiopia
et.dek: The Ethiopian Capital Market Authority has granted Deloitte a license to operate as an investment banking service provider, making it the second foreign firm to receive the permit.
paragraphs: Deloitte has secured an investment banking license from the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (ECMA), allowing it to offer non-brokerage services such as facilitating mergers and corporate organizations. This marks a significant step for the firm, which previously operated as a securities investment advisor after re-entering the Ethiopian market. The license was granted after a rigorous assessment process, according to the regulator.

The granting of this license makes Deloitte the second foreign entity to be authorized for investment banking services in Ethiopia, bringing the total number of licensed investment banks to nine. United Capital Financial Services Plc, a subsidiary of Nigeria's United Capital Group, was the first foreign firm to receive a similar license in June 2026. ECMA views these developments as a demonstration of confidence in Ethiopia's emerging financial ecosystem.

This upgrade from a Securities Investment Advisory role to an Investment Bank signifies growth and trust in the Ethiopian capital market, according to ECMA. The new license specifically permits Deloitte Ethiopia to engage in investment banking activities but does not allow it to act as a securities broker or dealer. The authority highlighted this transition as a positive indicator of the market's potential.

et.headline: National Bank Seeks Financial Tool Developer
et.dek: The National Bank of Ethiopia is inviting bids for the creation of a digital platform to compare financial product prices.
paragraphs: The National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) has issued an invitation for bids to develop a Financial Services Price Comparator Tool. This initiative aims to enhance transparency, protect consumers, and support informed financial decision-making within Ethiopia's expanding financial sector. The tool will be a regulator-led, non-commercial digital platform designed to allow consumers to easily access, compare, and understand the pricing and service features of various financial products.

The NBE is seeking a qualified consulting firm or consortium to design, develop, test, and implement the comparator tool. This project is supported by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) through its Rural Financial Intermediation Programme (RUFIP). The initiative aligns with national objectives to improve financial capability and inclusion, particularly for rural and underserved populations, by ensuring access to transparent and affordable financial services.

The bidding process is underway, with the bid closing date set for September 24, 2026, at 10:00 A.M., followed by the bid opening at 10:30 A.M. on the same day. The objective is to create a user-friendly and scalable digital platform that enables consumers to compare standardized financial products and pricing information across different institutions, thereby empowering them to make better financial choices.

et.headline: Ethiopia Delegates Back Executive Presidency Plan
et.dek: A national dialogue has endorsed constitutional changes that would merge the roles of prime minister and president into a powerful executive presidency.
paragraphs: Ethiopia's national dialogue has endorsed constitutional changes that would merge the roles of prime minister and president into a powerful executive presidency, a move critics warn could allow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed to further consolidate his control. More than 4,000 delegates participated in the weeks-long dialogue, which concluded on August 22. The delegates overwhelmingly backed a proposal to replace the current system with an executive presidency combining the powers of the prime minister and the largely ceremonial president.

The recommendations could be presented to parliament when it reconvenes in October. Although Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was absent from the dialogue, many observers expect him to be the leading candidate for the new position if the changes are adopted. The president would be chosen by a parliament dominated by members of his ruling party.

Supporters argue the proposal could create a more unifying national leadership, with the president representing all ethnic groups rather than being elected as a parliamentary representative. Opponents, however, fear the proposed changes could transform the political system to serve one individual, with political analyst Befekadu Hailu stating the reforms could effectively allow Abiy to assume the executive presidency while concentrating power in a single office.

gh.headline: Range Rover launches first electric model after year-long delay
gh.dek: The new electric vehicle, built in Solihull, represents a significant shift in the company's electrification strategy despite recent financial challenges.
paragraphs: Range Rover has unveiled its first fully electric model, the Range Rover Electric, following a year-long delay. The vehicle will be manufactured in Solihull, marking a substantial change in the company's electrification program. This initiative is supported by extensive upgrades to its West Midlands facilities.

Parent company JLR has trained ten thousand five hundred workers for electric production, proceeding with modernization despite financial pressures and planned job cuts. New battery and electric drive unit production lines are supporting the launch, with around nine thousand employees in Solihull and an additional one thousand five hundred across the region receiving electrification training.

JLR's Electric Propulsion Manufacturing Centre in Wolverhampton is now producing battery packs and electric drive units alongside internal combustion engines. This launch follows a turbulent year for the carmaker, which experienced falling profits and restructuring after a cyber attack last year.

gh.headline: Ghana Reference Rate Drops to 10.18% in September
gh.dek: The benchmark rate used by commercial banks to price loans saw a marginal decline, potentially easing borrowing costs for some customers.
paragraphs: The Ghana Reference Rate (GRR), a key benchmark for commercial bank lending, decreased to 10.18% in September 2026 from 10.61% in August. This 0.43 percentage-point reduction, calculated by JOYBUSINESS using industry data, was primarily driven by lower Treasury bill and interbank rates. The Bank of Ghana’s Monetary Policy Rate remained stable during this period.

This marginal drop in the GRR, which uses Treasury bill, interbank, and the Monetary Policy Rate in its calculation, could offer some relief to borrowers with variable-rate loans. While those with fixed rates will not see immediate changes, the development may encourage new borrowers as banks compete with lower advertised rates, with some customers reportedly accessing credit between 11% and 12.5%.

Introduced in 2017 by the Bank of Ghana and the Ghana Association of Banks, the GRR aims to provide a transparent benchmark for lending rates. The rate has shown fluctuations throughout 2026, moving from a high of 11.71% in March to lows around 10.02% in June, before its recent decline from August's 10.61% to September's 10.18%.

gh.headline: Shop owner fined for skipping sanitation day
gh.dek: A Hohoe Magistrate Court sentenced a shop owner to a GHS 240 fine or one month imprisonment for failing to participate in a mandatory clean-up exercise.
paragraphs: Esther Ofori, a provision shop owner in Hohoe, has been fined GHS 240 by the Hohoe Magistrate Court for refusing to participate in a communal clean-up exercise. The court also imposed a one-month jail sentence if the fine is not paid. Ofori pleaded guilty to the charge, which contravenes section 21 of the Hohoe Municipal Assembly bye-laws.

The clean-up exercise, organized by the Hohoe Municipal Assembly, is held on the first Thursday of every month between 0600 and 1000 hours as part of National Sanitation Day. During these hours, all businesses, except those providing emergency health or humanitarian services, are prohibited from operating. Business owners are required to use their own resources to clean their premises and surrounding areas, including desilting drains.

On July 2, 2026, at approximately 0922 hours, a Municipal Sanitation Taskforce observed Ofori operating her shop and selling to customers in the Atabu area. Her refusal to join the cleaning efforts led to her being served with a court summons. Environmental Health Analyst Daniel Dotse Eklo prosecuted the case before relieving judge Lambert Y. Keriba.

gh.headline: Davis convicted in Tupac Shakur murder case
gh.dek: Duane “Keffe D” Davis was found guilty of murder in Las Vegas, ending a 30-year-old case and raising questions about the unsolved murder of his rival, the Notorious B.I.G.
paragraphs: Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been convicted of the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas. The verdict follows a decades-long investigation into the drive-by shooting that killed Shakur. Prosecutors faced an uphill battle, with no eyewitnesses or murder weapon presented at trial, relying instead on Davis's own admissions in media appearances and a police interview.

The conviction of Davis, who admitted his nephew used a firearm he provided to shoot Shakur, brings closure to one of hip-hop's most enduring mysteries. This case's resolution has drawn parallels to the still-unsolved murder of Christopher Wallace, known as the Notorious B.I.G., who was killed in a similar drive-by shooting months after Shakur. Davis was present at a party the night Wallace was killed, and his connection to both cases has long been a subject of speculation.

The successful prosecution of Davis, despite the lack of traditional evidence, highlights the impact of his own words in cracking the cold case. Former prosecutor Neama Rahmani described the decision to charge Davis as a gutsy move, given the case's complexity and the passage of time. The connection between the two iconic rappers' deaths, both central figures in the 1990s East Coast-West Coast hip-hop rivalry, continues to fascinate observers.

gh.headline: Accused Threatener Granted GH¢100K Bail
gh.dek: A marketer accused of threatening Economic and Organised Crime Office staff has been granted bail, with his passport ordered deposited.
paragraphs: Kweku Osei Korankye Asiedu, a marketer, was granted GH¢100,000 bail with two sureties by an Accra Circuit Court. Asiedu faces charges including threat of death, offensive conduct, and publication of false information. He pleaded not guilty to all charges. The court also rescinded a previously issued bench warrant for his arrest and ordered him to report to the case investigator monthly.

The prosecution, led by Chief Inspector Wisdom Alorwu, stated that Asiedu was invited for questioning following a video circulated on social media in which he allegedly threatened EOCO staff. The video, recorded on May 29, 2026, reportedly contained statements like, “We know the officers’ houses, we know where they stay and will kill you.” Another video on July 13, 2026, allegedly falsely claimed an order from the Presidency to deny food to an individual in EOCO custody.

These alleged actions, according to the prosecution, were intended to provoke a breach of the peace and undermine EOCO officials' duties. The incidents reportedly instilled fear among EOCO personnel, with the driver of the Executive Director allegedly chased by unidentified men on motorbikes. Asiedu was arrested and allegedly admitted to the offences when cautioned.

The leaders identified agriculture, food security, water management, health services, technological innovation, security initiatives, and vocational training as priority areas for enhanced collaboration. President Tshisekedi emphasized the ambition to build a modern and pragmatic partnership with Israel, measured by the implementation and outcomes of joint projects.

cd.headline: Five Ebola Patients Recover and Leave Beni Treatment Centers
cd.dek: The largest group of recovered Ebola patients, including a caregiver, have been discharged from treatment centers in Beni, North Kivu.
paragraphs: Five patients, two children, two women, and a caregiver, have been released from Ebola treatment centers in Beni, North Kivu, after recovering from the virus. This marks the largest single group of recoveries discharged simultaneously from the two treatment facilities in Beni since the 17th Ebola epidemic began in May. The recoveries bring the total number of discharged patients from Beni's treatment centers to eleven since the outbreak started.

Dr. Jérémie Muhindo, head of the Ebola response commission in Beni, stated that these recoveries should reassure the public, emphasizing that prompt medical care leads to successful treatment. Survivors expressed immense joy and encouraged the population to trust healthcare workers and seek immediate consultation if symptoms appear. One survivor shared, "I came very weak, but now I am truly in shape. Thank you to the healthcare staff and may God bless them!"

Another recovered patient stated, "I am happy. I came in a sick state, today I am cured. The big message is that the population must become aware that the disease exists and that they should come for treatment." The discharged patients are now in good health and have left the treatment centers, offering hope and encouraging community engagement with healthcare services.

cd.headline: DR Congo Census Uses Digital Tools and Satellite Imagery
cd.dek: The technical coordinator of the Central Census Bureau announced that the operation relies on digital tools and satellite imagery to map the population.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo is undertaking a nationwide mapping operation to better understand its population and plan for development. Henri Marie Kazadi, technical coordinator for the Central Census Bureau, stated that the census is essential for national progress and that development cannot wait. This initiative employs digital tools and satellite imagery, marking a significant technological shift for the country's demographic data collection.

Kazadi emphasized the need for broad public participation, calling it a guarantee for the success of the census operations. This census is the first to be conducted in 42 years, following the one organized in 1984 during the era of Zaire. The current operation aims to establish a reliable demographic database for the Congolese population.

Participants in a Radio Okapi broadcast, hosted by Jean Marc Matwaki Mofelele, stressed the importance of transparency and the reliability of the results. They also highlighted the necessity of large-scale public awareness campaigns to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the demographic data being collected.

cd.headline: Congolese Influencer Arrested in Tanzania on International Warrant
cd.dek: Tanzanian authorities apprehended Denise Dusauchoy on August 30, 2026, following a request from the Democratic Republic of Congo's justice ministry.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ministry of Justice confirmed the arrest of Congolese influencer Denise Dusauchoy, also known as Denise Mukendi, in Tanzania on August 30, 2026. The arrest occurred as part of an international judicial cooperation procedure. Tanzanian authorities detained Dusauchoy based on an arrest warrant issued by Congolese judicial authorities.

This operation follows judicial actions initiated in criminal cases under investigation since 2025. The Ministry of Justice highlighted the "diligent collaboration" of Tanzanian authorities. The ministry also stated that the arrest is a procedural step and does not prejudge the individual's guilt, emphasizing her right to the presumption of innocence until a final judicial decision.

The proceedings leading to the arrest began in 2025 when the Prosecutor General near the Court of Cassation sent three international rogatory letters to Belgian judicial authorities. These requests pertained to criminal cases opened at the Kinshasa/Gombe High Court of Justice, involving Dusauchoy and others, for which international arrest warrants had been issued.

tz.headline: Tanzania Digital Health Push Adds AI, Hospital Tech to Procurement
tz.dek: The nation's healthcare sector is embracing digital transformation, with electronic records and artificial intelligence shaping service delivery and creating new market.
paragraphs: Tanzania's healthcare sector is entering a new phase of digital transformation, integrating electronic medical records, interoperable health information systems, and artificial intelligence. This shift is creating new opportunities for technology providers, distributors, and investors as the country aims to strengthen data use and digital tools across its health system. The Ministry of Health is advancing digital health through initiatives focused on interoperability and the digitalization of primary healthcare, supporting systems that improve data access for clinical and management decisions.

Electronic medical record coverage has reached 100% in national and referral hospitals, with significant adoption expanding across district facilities. Healthcare providers are increasingly seeking technologies to improve diagnosis, patient management, and operational efficiency, with AI applications for disease surveillance and diagnostics being explored. The Afya-Tek digital system, launched in December 2024, aims to strengthen community-level healthcare services.

The World Health Expo (WHX) 2026 in Nairobi will convene healthcare technology providers, hospital decision-makers, and investors as Tanzanian organizations evaluate technologies based on practical outcomes. Interoperability remains a critical consideration, with programs emphasizing secure data exchange across health facilities to enhance patient history access, hospital management, and clinical support.

tz.headline: Tanzania Regulator Slashes Fuel Prices for September
tz.dek: The Energy and Water Utilities Regulatory Authority announced a significant drop in petrol and diesel costs, effective September 2.
paragraphs: The Energy and Water Utilities Regulatory Authority (EWURA) has reduced the prices of petroleum products for September 2026. Petrol prices have fallen by 102/- per litre, and diesel by 101/- per litre. These new prices, effective from September 2, 2026, apply to fuel dealers operating under Tanzania’s regulated indicative pricing system.

EWURA stated it is closely monitoring global oil market developments, which are influenced by factors such as the security situation in the Middle East. Under the Petroleum Act of 2015, fuel prices in Tanzania are determined by a market-based system, but retail dealers must not exceed EWURA's set indicative prices.

The regulatory body has also called on the public to assist in monitoring compliance by reporting any fuel stations found selling petroleum products above the prescribed indicative prices. This move aims to ensure fair pricing for consumers across the country.

tz.headline: Arusha Police Detain Activist; Accounts of Detention Differ
tz.dek: Human rights activist Godlisten Malisa was detained at the Namanga border post on August 31, with his account of events contradicting the police's official statement.
paragraphs: Arusha police confirmed on Tuesday the detention of activist Godlisten Elisante Malisa at the Namanga border post on August 31. Police stated Malisa and another unidentified individual were arrested on "criminal allegations under investigation" and later released on bail. This official account follows hours of uncertainty after Malisa's lawyer and a friend reported him missing from the border crossing.

Malisa, however, stated he was not bailed out and did not post bail, asserting he was not investigated for any criminal charges. He reported spending the night in a holding cell at the Diplomacy and Tourism Police Station in Arusha after being taken from the border by five individuals identifying as police officers. He claimed they initially acted courteously and he was not mistreated.

The activist recounted arriving at Namanga after his flight from the United States was rerouted due to industrial action in Kenya. He stated Tanzanian officials could not read his passport, leading to a delay. His lawyer reported he was removed by individuals not in uniform. Malisa's belongings were returned when he left the station on September 1.

tz.dek: A Member of Parliament has asked for the government's strategy to ensure the driving profession gains dignity and respect equal to other careers.
paragraphs: Dodoma: Rashid Shangazi, the Member of Parliament for Mlalo, questioned in parliament the government's strategy to ensure the driving profession achieves dignity, status, and respect comparable to other careers. He sought to understand the measures in place to elevate the profession.

Responding to the inquiry, Regina Qwaray, the Deputy Minister in the President's Office for Public Service Management and Good Governance, stated that the government has taken various steps to ensure the driving profession is accorded the same dignity and respect as other careers. She affirmed the government's commitment to this goal.

The Deputy Minister detailed that the government is improving the career development structure for drivers, enhancing professional training and educational standards, and strengthening incentives and welfare for the driving cadre. These actions aim to meet and manage the demands of the working environment for drivers.

ma.headline: Morocco Bars Convicted Candidates From 2026 Elections
ma.dek: New rules disqualify individuals with first-instance or final convictions on appeal from running, strengthening electoral integrity.
paragraphs: Morocco's upcoming 2026 parliamentary elections will enforce stricter candidate eligibility, barring those convicted of offenses that undermine electoral ethics. Candidacies can be rejected or annulled if violations are confirmed after submission. Individuals with first-instance convictions for serious charges, or final convictions on appeal leading to loss of eligibility, will also be ineligible to run.

These measures are part of a strengthened legal framework designed to ensure electoral integrity, fair competition, and transparency, aiming to restore public trust in elected bodies. The reforms also extend the ban for officials removed from office to two full electoral terms, preventing their swift return to public service after misconduct.

Penalties for electoral crimes are toughened, with increased prison terms and financial penalties, and some violations now classified as crimes. The legislation also addresses digital risks, criminalizing the use of social media, online platforms, and AI for electoral fraud, including spreading false information or manipulating content. Paid political advertisements on foreign platforms are banned to prevent external influence.

ma.headline: King's Visit Threatens Morocco-Spain Dispute Over Ceuta, Melilla
ma.dek: A planned royal visit to Spanish enclaves on Morocco's coast could reignite a decades-old territorial dispute, according to a Moroccan official.
paragraphs: A planned visit by Spain’s King Felipe VI to the North African cities of Ceuta and Melilla could reignite tensions with Morocco, according to Yahya Yahya, head of a Moroccan committee campaigning for the territories’ return. Yahya stated the visit could trigger a stronger reaction than a similar trip in 2007 by Spain’s former King Juan Carlos I and Queen Sofia, which sparked widespread anger and condemnation. He warned that a new visit could provoke an even stronger response and said the Spanish government would bear responsibility for any consequences.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez confirmed King Felipe VI plans to visit both cities, citing “sufficient arguments and reasons” and appropriate conditions, though no date was announced. Yahya, who heads the Committee for the Liberation of Ceuta, Melilla and their affiliated islands, described the territories as an “existential” issue for Morocco, comparable to the Western Sahara issue. He accused Spanish leaders of reviving a sensitive dispute and vowed his committee would be present to reaffirm Morocco's claim.

Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish territories on Morocco’s northern coast, which Morocco considers part of its territory while Spain maintains sovereignty. The dispute arises as Spain and Morocco have sought to strengthen bilateral ties in recent years, particularly on migration and security cooperation. Sanchez described cooperation with Morocco on migration as “very positive.”

ma.headline: Moroccan Jewish community urges election turnout, abstains from endorsements
ma.dek: Community representatives stated that voting decisions are personal and should reflect each citizen’s preferred political program, rejecting a separate electoral bloc.
paragraphs: Morocco’s Jewish community is encouraging its members to participate in the upcoming September 23 parliamentary election, but will not endorse any specific party or candidate. Community representatives emphasized that voting choices are personal and should align with individual political preferences, discouraging the idea of Jewish Moroccans acting as a distinct electoral bloc with unique demands.

Jacky Kadoch, president of the Jewish community in the Marrakech-Safi region, stated that political parties should serve Jewish citizens under the same policies and commitments applied to all Moroccans, without requiring special platform measures. He noted that matters concerning Jewish institutions have traditionally been managed through the Interior Ministry and praised the state's support for preserving Jewish heritage sites.

Kadoch estimated that fewer than 2,000 to 2,200 Jewish people currently reside in Morocco, with some areas having only 20 to 30 community members. Eligible voters living abroad can participate via the proxy voting system available to registered Moroccans overseas.

ma.headline: Amrabat Joins FC Utrecht on Free Transfer
ma.dek: Veteran forward Nordin Amrabat, 39, signed with FC Utrecht after departing Wydad AC, with his brother's influence playing a key role.
paragraphs: Dutch Eredivisie club FC Utrecht has officially signed 39-year-old forward Nordin Amrabat on a free transfer. The move takes immediate effect, making him eligible for upcoming matches after training with the squad. Amrabat joins the club following his departure from Moroccan side Wydad AC.

The transfer was influenced by his brother, former FC Utrecht midfielder Sofyan Amrabat, who contacted technical director Jordy Zuidam. FC Utrecht management expressed enthusiasm, highlighting Amrabat's career at PSV Eindhoven, Galatasaray, Málaga, and Watford. Amrabat shared his pride, calling the move the 'cherry on the cake' of his career.

Amrabat noted his family's connection to the club through his brother's time in the youth academy and their excitement to return to Stadion Galgenwaard. He will now aim to make an immediate impact for FC Utrecht, which is currently 17th in the Eredivisie standings.

ma.headline: UN Rights Team Assesses Moroccan Ombudsman's Work
ma.dek: A United Nations human rights delegation visited Laayoune to review mediation and citizen rights protection mechanisms.
paragraphs: An international human rights delegation, led by Teresa McCordy of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, met with officials at the Moroccan Ombudsman Institution's regional office in Laayoune. The visit focused on understanding the office's role in mediation, redress, and safeguarding citizens' rights when dealing with public authorities. Cherif Laroussi, the regional delegate, provided an overview of the office's functions, including complaint processing and inter-governmental communication.

Discussions during the visit centered on enhancing the accessibility of mediation and redress systems for citizens and strengthening the protection of rights. The delegation and Moroccan officials also explored avenues for improving the quality of public services. Moulay Lahcen Naji, chairman of the Independent Commission for Human Rights in Africa, also attended the meeting, underscoring the collaborative nature of the exchange.

McCordy showed particular interest in the regional office's methods for handling complaints and its communication strategies with public institutions. This engagement is part of wider initiatives aimed at fostering cooperation and sharing best practices in human rights and mediation.

ug.headline: Man shot during Uganda National Cleaning Day operation
ug.dek: Kizito Ronald Jjuuko, 38, died after being shot from behind by police during a National Cleaning Day event.
paragraphs: A 38-year-old boda boda rider, husband, and father, Kizito Ronald Jjuuko, was killed during a police operation on August 29. Jjuuko was shot from behind while police enforced movement restrictions during the second National Cleaning Day. The incident has raised questions about the methods used to ensure compliance with the national initiative.

The National Cleaning Day, aimed at addressing visible refuse in the capital, was met with both support and skepticism due to a perceived trust deficit between the government and citizens. Previous events have seen controversial police actions, including reports of officers using excessive force against individuals during the first cleaning day in July.

Jjuuko's death, described as occurring in "needless circumstances," highlights concerns over the police's approach to enforcing public order during civic initiatives. The incident has prompted calls for an immediate review of the operational procedures employed during these national events.

ug.headline: Uganda Halts New Mineral Licenses for One Month
ug.dek: The government aims to tighten oversight and ensure mineral wealth benefits the nation by pausing new grants for exploration and mining.
paragraphs: Uganda has imposed a one-month moratorium on issuing new mineral licenses and exploration rights, a move announced by Energy Minister Dr. Monica Musenero Masanza. This temporary freeze is intended to tighten government oversight, eliminate speculative claims, and align the mining sector with the country's economic transformation agenda. The minister described the suspension as a regulatory reset, emphasizing the goal of ensuring Uganda's mineral wealth translates into greater domestic value, job creation, and public revenue.

The intervention places the mining sector at the core of Uganda's Tenfold Growth Strategy, which targets an economy of approximately US$500 billion by 2040. Minerals are identified as a priority sector alongside agro-industrialization, tourism, and science, technology, and innovation. This aligns with the Fourth National Development Plan (NDP IV), which prioritizes value addition, industrialization, employment, and private sector growth as key economic drivers.

This moratorium follows a significant expansion in mineral licensing, particularly after the introduction of the digital Mining Cadastre and Registry System. By June 30, 2026, the ministry had granted 212 prospecting licenses, 497 exploration licenses, and various other mining, smelting, refining, processing, and dealer licenses. The Directorate of Geological Survey and Mines acknowledges ongoing data cleaning and system migration as part of the digital system's transition.

ug.headline: Uganda parishes become agro-industrial nodes
ug.dek: Government shifts focus for Parish Development Model funds from financing to value-addition hubs for agricultural products.
paragraphs: The Ugandan government is re-envisioning its Parish Development Model (PDM) parishes as potential agro-industrial nodes, moving beyond their current role as financing units. Since 2022, Shs 4.4 trillion has been disbursed to 10,589 parishes to boost production, with over three million people receiving funds by June 2026. However, the government recognizes that simply increasing production is insufficient for sustained household income growth, especially for farmers selling unprocessed goods who face low prices and post-harvest losses.

Value addition is identified as crucial for agro-industrialization, improving product quality, extending shelf life, and accessing higher-value markets. While past programs invested in processing facilities like maize mills and coffee hullers, adoption remains limited due to issues such as unreliable electricity, weak management, and poor market linkages. The government's 2026/27 budget allocates significant funds to agro-industrialization, transport, and energy, aiming to address these infrastructure gaps and support parish-level production and processing systems.

The PDM's integrated design, with pillars focusing on agricultural value chains and infrastructure, should synergize to support value addition and commercialization. Instead of large processing plants in every parish, the strategy suggests Parish SACCOs and producer groups can aggregate produce and operate shared facilities like solar dryers or grain mills on a fee-for-service basis. Infrastructure development should prioritize areas with high production potential and strong market links.

ug.headline: Conservationists Restore Forest Corridor for Uganda's Chimpanzees
ug.dek: ECOTRUST and partners are securing and restoring over 50,000 hectares of forest to reconnect isolated chimpanzee populations.
paragraphs: Environmental groups are working to restore a vital forest corridor in Western Uganda to protect the country's endangered eastern chimpanzees. The Budongo-Bugoma landscape, home to approximately 5,000 chimpanzees, has been fragmented by agricultural expansion and oil development, isolating wildlife. The Environmental Conservation Trust of Uganda (ECOTRUST) is leading an initiative to conserve and reconnect over 50,000 hectares of natural forest across Kikuube, Hoima, and Masindi districts.

The project aims to re-establish critical ecological linkages between the Bugoma and Budongo forest reserves, which are essential for the free movement of wildlife. Historically, a lack of sustainable funding has hampered restoration efforts. ECOTRUST, through its Northern Albertine Rift Conservation Group (NARC-G), secured foundational support from the World Land Trust in 2020 and mobilized additional resources in 2022 from IUCN Netherlands and Total Energies to implement the corridor restoration plan.

This restoration is crucial for the long-term survival of the eastern chimpanzee population, preventing genetic isolation. The region is a biodiversity hotspot, supporting 52% of Africa’s bird species and 39% of its mammal species, alongside other primates. The initiative addresses severe environmental pressures that have turned a continuous forest belt into isolated patches on community and private lands.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe Banks Offer Car Loans as Safe Lending Option
zw.dek: Despite a stable financial sector, high borrowing costs prevent many working Zimbabweans from financing new vehicles.
paragraphs: Zimbabwean banks are increasingly offering vehicle asset finance, viewing it as a secure lending avenue. A financed vehicle provides lenders with tangible collateral and a clear repayment case, making it attractive in a cautious credit market. Banks are under pressure to increase lending, and vehicle finance has emerged as a safer option for expanding credit portfolios, moving beyond transactional income towards more productive lending that supports economic activity.

The banking sector's financial health appears robust, with total loans and advances reaching ZiG55.93 billion by December 31, 2024, and foreign-currency loans dominating at 88.17%. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 29.69% in 2025, well above the 12% regulatory minimum, and the non-performing loans ratio was 3.47%, below the 5% benchmark. These figures indicate a stable and liquid sector, though one that remains cautious in its lending practices.

However, this caution contrasts sharply with the accessibility of credit in neighboring South Africa, where individuals can secure substantial loans for cars and homes. In Zimbabwe, many employed citizens face prohibitively high borrowing costs, making new vehicle financing economically unviable. Consequently, the rational choice for many is to purchase used vehicles with cash, highlighting a weakness in the credit market where finance exists but on terms that often negate its purpose for ordinary citizens.

zw.headline: Council Bulldozers Demolish Homes Amidst Fears of Operation Murambatsvina
zw.dek: Local authorities are razing structures in informal settlements, leaving thousands of families with uncertain futures and sparking fears of a repeat of past demolitions.
paragraphs: Local authorities have intensified demolitions of structures in informal settlements, leading to ruined lives and shattered dreams for thousands of families. Recent tours by the Local Government minister and Harare City Council officials have sent tremors through residents, raising fears of a looming Operation Murambatsvina. Structures in St Martins, near Sunningdale, were razed down about two weeks ago, following similar demolitions in Ridgeview, Belvedere in 2024, and Stoneridge this year.

Council officials argue that the targeted properties lack municipal approval or legal title deeds, or are situated on prohibited sites such as wetlands, road reserves, and land designated for public facilities. Residents are often victims of land barons and politicians who sell them land using fraudulent paperwork, only for municipal officials to later demolish the costly structures, sometimes after officials had watched them being built. These land barons and politicians often collude with corrupt municipal officials, creating a false sense of legitimacy for residents.

The demolitions are reportedly expected to extend to Budiriro, Kuwadzana, Glen View, Mabvuku, and Greendale. Authorities are urged to move away from a reactive approach and implement routine inspections to verify the legality of construction activities before residents invest their life savings in structures that could be demolished. This would prevent families from being thrown into desperation and facing inclement weather.

zw.headline: Afreximbank Appoints New Regional Leaders, Names Harare Director
zw.dek: The African Export-Import Bank has named Peter Adeshola Olowononi as director for Southern Africa, based in Harare, as part of a wider leadership reshuffle.
paragraphs: Afreximbank has appointed Peter Adeshola Olowononi as director, regional operations, Southern Africa, with his base in Harare. Olowononi will lead the bank’s operations, client coverage, and strategic engagement in the region. His prior role was director, client relations, Anglophone West Africa, and he brings experience in client coverage and transaction origination to this new position.

This appointment is part of a broader leadership restructuring aimed at strengthening Afreximbank’s presence in key regional markets to foster intra-African trade, industrialization, and integration. The bank stated that these changes are intended to enhance regional operations, improve client engagement, and expedite transaction execution across Africa and the Caribbean. Other appointments include Eric Intong Monchu as group managing director in Cairo and Roy Reid as chief operating officer for the Caribbean office in Barbados.

The bank noted that many of the newly appointed executives have advanced from within Afreximbank, bringing valuable institutional knowledge and established client relationships. These appointments align with the bank's ongoing expansion in financing trade and economic development across Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the internal talent pool and supporting the bank's development mandate, according to Afreximbank president George Elombi.

zw.headline: Harare to Host 19th Comesa Business Forum
zw.dek: Zimbabwean businesses will connect with regional buyers and investors at the forum, held alongside the Comesa Heads of State Summit.
paragraphs: Harare will host the 19th Comesa Business Forum and Multi-Sectoral International Exhibition from October 19 to 21, 2026. The event, convened by the Comesa Business Council, ZimTrade, and the Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce, aims to boost intra-regional trade and investment. It will bring together businesses, financial institutions, development partners, and government representatives from across the Comesa region, which encompasses over 640 million people and a US$1 trillion GDP.

The forum, running under the theme “One Market, One Future: Advancing Inclusive Industrialisation, Investment and Regional Integration in Comesa,” will focus on strengthening regional value chains, expanding productive capacity, and promoting value addition. Structured business-to-business and business-to-government engagements are planned to foster partnerships and transactions. A private sector communiqué with recommendations for the Comesa Summit is expected.

Discussions will cover seamless trade systems, reducing non-tariff barriers, and strengthening trade corridors. Access to finance, reducing investment risks, and leveraging digital technologies will also be addressed. A Multi-Sectoral International Exhibition will run concurrently, featuring country pavilions and networking platforms, with priority sectors including manufacturing, agriculture, and financial services.

cv.headline: Government Prepares Drought Mitigation Program
cv.dek: A new integrated plan will address animal watering and food deficits while supporting vulnerable families.
paragraphs: The Cape Verdean government is developing a comprehensive program to mitigate the effects of climate change, specifically targeting drought scenarios. Minister Eveline Ramos stated that the initiative will not only provide for animal watering and food needs but also offer income support to vulnerable households. This proactive approach is necessary given the nation's high vulnerability to climate fluctuations, which can lead to extreme weather events like floods or prolonged dry spells. The program aims to create resilience against these varied climatic conditions.

Beyond climate change impacts, the agricultural sector faces a structural challenge with the emigration of young people, leading to a shortage of labor. This exodus is expected to reduce the total cultivated area. The ministry is working on strategies to re-engage youth in the primary sector, recognizing the critical role they play in ensuring future agricultural productivity and food security.

The minister also reflected on the National Program for Agricultural Investment and Food Security (PNIASAN) from 2015-2025, deeming its first phase successful in poverty reduction, strengthening food security, and fostering agricultural development. Separately, the Ministry of Agriculture announced a public tender for the sale of donated rice from the Japanese government.

cv.headline: Brazilian Dancers Bring Contemporary Performances to Praia
cv.dek: Two Brazilian artists will present contemporary dance solos at the Centro Cultural Português as part of the KORDA artistic exchange program.
paragraphs: Praia will host two contemporary dance performances on Friday, September fourth, at the Centro Cultural Português. The event, part of the KORDA artistic exchange initiative, aims to foster artist circulation, creative process sharing, and dialogue between different cultural contexts. The free performances, starting at 18:30, will feature Brazilian choreographer and dancer Karla Mendes with her solo "Território de Travessia" and dancer and performer Ricardo Aparecido with "Re-Traços."

The participation of these two Brazilian artists is a result of the Funarte Conexões Internacionais Program, establishing an artistic exchange partnership between Brazil and Cape Verde. Mendes's work explores the experience of being a woman through lunar archetypes, focusing on body as a territory for creation and belonging. Aparecido's performance integrates movement, voice, sound, and light in a constantly transforming environment, building its narrative through chance and interaction.

Karla Mendes, with over two decades of experience, researches Afro-diasporic dances and the connection between body, ancestry, and spirituality. Ricardo Aparecido is a contemporary dancer, performer, and creator who blends his practice with Contact Improvisation, Capoeira Angola, and performance art. Both artists bring unique perspectives and extensive backgrounds to this cultural exchange.

cv.headline: Cape Verde Government to Remove Children from Prison System
cv.dek: The justice minister announced plans to transform the Orlando Pantera center into a socio-educational facility focused on youth rehabilitation.
paragraphs: The Cape Verdean government intends to separate the Orlando Pantera Center from the prison system and establish a dedicated socio-educational directorate. This move aims to focus on the education and reintegration of children and young people, according to the Minister of Justice. The minister stated a clear desire to avoid incarceration for individuals aged 12 to 16, advocating for the center to become a place of "education and re-education" rather than a holding facility.

The first step involves removing the Orlando Pantera Center from the current prison administration, followed by the creation of a distinct direction for the socio-educational system. The minister also expressed his intention to involve specialized professionals to foster a significantly different environment for the young residents. The Orlando Pantera Socio-Educational Center, established in December 2005, is a public institution tasked with implementing socio-educational protective measures for minors in conflict with the law.

The minister articulated that the Orlando Pantera Socio-Educational Center has no place within the prison system's structure, as it does not align with its objectives. He emphasized the need for a center that actively educates and rehabilitates children and youth, rather than simply detaining them and preparing them for further involvement with the penal system. The goal is to create a supportive and corrective environment, distinct from punitive measures.

td.headline: Chad Security Ministry Bans Police Intervention in Community Disputes
td.dek: A directive from the Ministry of Public Security prohibits all internal security forces from engaging in community conflicts, threatening disciplinary action.
paragraphs: Chad's Ministry of Public Security has issued a formal order forbidding members of the Internal Security Forces (FSI) from intervening in community disputes. Minister Ali Ahmat Akhabach signed the directive on September 1, 2026, in N'Djamena, emphasizing that any violation will result in severe disciplinary sanctions.

The ban applies to all FSI personnel, including generals, senior and junior officers, non-commissioned officers, peacekeepers, and soldiers. The ministry has tasked the directors general of the National Police, National Gendarmerie, Intelligence and Investigations, and the commander of the National and Nomad Guard with ensuring strict adherence to this new policy.

This measure aims to prevent security forces from becoming involved in local disagreements. The directive serves as a clear warning against any form of interference by law enforcement in the resolution of community-based conflicts across the country.

td.headline: Prosecutor seeks one year jail for fraud defendant
td.dek: A N'Djamena court heard a fraud case where the prosecutor requested a one-year prison sentence and a fine.
paragraphs: The N'Djamena High Court on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, heard a case involving a defendant at the Klessoum detention center. The prosecutor dropped charges of forgery and uttering a forged document, proceeding only with fraud. He requested a one-year prison sentence and a fine of one hundred thousand FCFA for the public treasury.

The dispute originated from a partnership between the defendant and a local association involved in fundraising. The plaintiff claims the defendant defrauded them of over three hundred million FCFA. However, the defense lawyer disputes this amount, calling it imaginary and stating the actual transaction volume was seventy million FCFA.

The defense argued that the plaintiff filed multiple complaints and that their client is a victim of a scam by an "untouchable" third party whose testimony the court refused to hear. The defense claims the plaintiff and this third party are artificially inflating the debt to hold the defendant solely responsible. The court has reserved its decision for a future hearing.

td.headline: Defense Seeks Acquittal for Abdoulaye Miskine
td.dek: The second day of Abdoulaye Miskine's trial heard testimony from co-accused as civil parties demanded reparations for alleged war crimes.
paragraphs: The second day of Abdoulaye Miskine's trial on Tuesday, September 1, focused on the testimony of co-accused individuals. The Coordination of Civil Society Associations and Human Rights Defense (Cascidho), acting as a civil party, reiterated accusations of torture, rape, and forced disappearance, seeking reparations for victims. Miskine's defense team characterized the proceedings as fitting and outlined a strategy for acquittal, centering on an objection to the court's jurisdiction raised by the main defendant.

Mahamat Digadimbaye, coordinator for Cascidho, stated that his organization filed the complaint against Abdoulaye Miskine and others, citing crimes against humanity including torture, rape, and forced disappearance. He emphasized that the Chadian people expect justice and that Miskine operated as a warlord at the border, causing atrocities that left hundreds of victims unable to attend the trial. Cascidho, which initially filed a complaint in 2020, is seeking damages for the harm suffered by victims due to the actions of Miskine's elements.

The trial is proceeding with contradictory exchanges between parties as interrogations continue. Cascidho's involvement as a civil party since 2020 highlights allegations of kidnappings, unlawful detentions, cattle theft, rape, and assassinations committed within Chadian territory. The defense is preparing its case for acquittal, focusing on procedural arguments regarding the court's authority to hear the case.

td.headline: Xi Jinping Calls for Enhanced Development and Security at SCO Summit
td.dek: Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined a vision for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization focused on shared prosperity, regional security, and equitable global governance.
paragraphs: At the 26th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Council of Heads of State in Bishkek, Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasized the organization's quarter-century of existence. He addressed fellow leaders, including Kyrgyzstan's Sadyr Japarov and Uzbekistan's Chavkat Mirziyoïev, recalling the foundational principles of mutual trust, shared benefit, and non-confrontation that define the Shanghai Spirit.

Amidst contemporary geopolitical challenges and international tensions, President Xi articulated a four-point plan. This vision prioritizes development and common prosperity, strengthens regional security, centers on peoples to consolidate cultural ties, and promotes more equitable global governance. China pledges to make the SCO a priority region for its Belt and Road Initiative, proposing an international AI cooperation center and increased renewable energy capacity.

The summit also marked the transition of the SCO presidency to Pakistan, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif accepting the role. China committed to implementing numerous technological and educational projects within the SCO framework over the next three years, aiming to foster deeper cooperation and development among member states.

dj.headline: Djibouti Customs Modernizes with Electronic Single Window
dj.dek: A new electronic single window system aims to simplify customs procedures, reduce delays, and improve transparency in trade operations.
paragraphs: Djibouti's national customs administration is accelerating its modernization by establishing an electronic single window system. This initiative, developed with partners including the Ministry of Commerce, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat, and the Korean agency Cupia, seeks to streamline trade processes. Cupia has prior experience implementing similar systems in Ethiopia, Tanzania, and Ghana.

The launch of this project was marked by a workshop held at the People's Palace, attended by key figures such as Mr. Ali Abdou Daoud, Secretary General of the Ministry of Commerce, and Mr. Abdourahman Izzi Awad, a senior customs official. Representatives from AfCFTA and Cupia were also present, underscoring the collaborative nature of the project.

According to Mr. Izzi, the goal extends beyond enhancing the current SYDONIAWORLD system. The electronic single window is intended to simplify customs and trade formalities, cut down processing times, boost transparency, and increase the predictability of operations. This aligns with the AfCFTA's objectives of fostering economic integration and facilitating intra-African trade.

dj.headline: Djibouti AI Adoption Accelerates Beyond Measurement
dj.dek: The nation is transitioning from discovering artificial intelligence to integrating it into daily life and administration.
paragraphs: Djibouti is moving beyond the initial discovery phase of artificial intelligence and is now increasingly integrating AI into daily life, administration, higher education, and businesses. However, the pace of AI adoption is outpacing the country's ability to measure its impact, according to Dr. Houssein Ahmed Assoweh. A national survey to precisely quantify AI usage, its applications, and effects among Djiboutians is currently lacking, making it scientifically challenging to provide exact figures.

Favorable conditions for AI diffusion are present, including strong international connectivity, the expansion of digital public services, increasing use of digital platforms, and administrative modernization. The University of Djibouti, through structures like the Centre for Research in Mathematics and Digitalization, is developing skills in mathematical modeling, data science, and artificial intelligence. Scientific work is underway on areas such as Somali language processing, climate modeling, and machine learning applications relevant to the country.

Dr. Assoweh emphasizes that Djibouti must shift from merely consuming AI tools developed elsewhere to becoming a producer of data, skills, research, and AI solutions tailored to national priorities. This requires strengthening existing digital, legal, scientific, and institutional foundations, which are currently fragmented. Recommendations include integrating AI and ethics into curricula, enhancing specialized training, and establishing a national AI center of excellence with dedicated research funding to build a critical mass of local expertise.

sz.headline: Home Affairs Official Found Guilty in ID Fraud Case
sz.dek: A Civil Service Commission ruling found an official guilty of illegally issuing an Eswatini ID and birth certificate to a South African businessman.
paragraphs: The Civil Service Commission (CSC) has found a Home Affairs official guilty of unlawfully processing an Eswatini birth certificate and national identity card for South African businessman Vusi ‘Cat’ Matlala. The CSC described the actions of suspended Assistant Regional Civil Registrar Nonhlanhla Malambe as a serious breach that compromised national security and border integrity.

Malambe was charged with dishonesty for registering Matlala’s birth on February 12, 2024, under the name Vusimuzi Dlamini, falsely listing Thembi Christinah Zulu as the mother. She then issued an identity card on February 20, 2024, without requiring necessary source documents. Malambe admitted to bypassing protocols, claiming she was misled by an individual she trusted.

The commission stressed the registration was a deliberate violation, not an error, noting that standard late registration procedures, including a letter from the relevant umphakatsi and verification of the informant’s relationship to the registrant, were entirely bypassed. The ruling raises concerns about the integrity of the country’s civil registration system and the potential for other fraudulent documents.

sz.headline: Police Probe Maize Smuggling Syndicate
sz.dek: Authorities have intercepted two truckloads of white maize suspected of being illegally imported from South Africa.
paragraphs: The Royal Eswatini Police Service, in collaboration with the National Maize Corporation, is investigating a suspected syndicate involved in smuggling tonnes of white maize into Eswatini from South Africa. Two consignments were intercepted at the Ngwenya Border Gate, with trucks detained as investigations into their origin, ownership, and documentation continue. The National Maize Corporation has intensified its monitoring and scrutiny of maize imports to protect the regulated supply chain.

Regulations under the National Agricultural Marketing Board Act and the Control of Cereals Act require permits for importing maize, with only the National Maize Corporation currently authorized to do so. Bongani Mdluli, NAMBoard Head of Legal Trade and Regulation, confirmed the interceptions, expressing concern over broken laws and stating that one case is now in court. He noted that one intercepted entity lacked a permit and failed to declare the consignment.

Mdluli suggested the two interceptions within two weeks could indicate a larger problem, potentially the "tip of the iceberg" of a smuggling syndicate. NAMBoard is reportedly tightening its regulatory measures, though specific actions will not be publicly disclosed. The illegal importation of maize can lead to fines, penalties, and seizure of goods.

sz.headline: Muzi brace sinks Ally’s rebranded Amawele
sz.dek: Manzini Sea Birds launched their new season with a 2-0 victory over Ally Kgomongwe’s Amawele in the 8Bet Trade Fair Cup.
paragraphs: Manzini Sea Birds began their new season with a 2-0 win against Ally Kgomongwe’s Amawele in the 8Bet Trade Fair Cup at Mavuso Sports Centre. The victory propels Sea Birds into the quarter-finals, where they will face Green Mamba. Amawele, who are awaiting approval to change their name to Mbabane Black Eagles for the 2027/28 season, were unable to score despite creating chances.

Veteran forward Muzi Tsabedze scored both goals for Sea Birds, opening the scoring three minutes after halftime and sealing the win with his second goal 11 minutes from full time. Amawele’s Wandile Ntsakala forced a save from Sea Birds goalkeeper Ntokozo Shabangu with a long-range effort. Sea Birds’ new recruits, including Mncedisi ‘Mpotho’ Dlamini, featured in the match.

The win marks a strong start for Manzini Sea Birds, who finished as league runners-up last season. Amawele, under new ownership by Kgomongwe, showed potential but lacked the finishing touch. The match saw Sea Birds advance to the next stage of the cup competition, while Amawele were eliminated.

sz.headline: Two new radio stations receive operating licences
sz.dek: Eswatini Communications Commission awarded free-to-air commercial radio broadcasting service licences to Sakha Live FM and Icon Connect Radio.
paragraphs: The Eswatini broadcasting sector is set to expand with the official handover of operating licences to Sakha Live FM and Icon Connect Radio. The Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) presented the two stations with their free-to-air commercial radio broadcasting service licences yesterday. These licences were issued following an invitation to apply published by ESCCOM in December 2025, marking a significant step in the liberalisation of the sector.

ESCCOM Acting Chief Executive Officer Ozzie Thakatha stated that the new broadcasters are expected to introduce greater content diversity, innovative approaches, and new technologies, fostering increased audience engagement and a wider range of opinions. Thakatha also highlighted the potential for economic opportunities through employment in various roles, benefiting the wider creative industry including independent producers, musicians, and advertising agencies. The stations have 12 months from the licence award date to commence operations.

Sakha Live FM Managing Director Melusi ‘Zox’ Dlamini expressed excitement about the licence, emphasizing the station's aim to be more than an entertainment platform. He stated Sakha Live will connect listeners, businesses, and young people to opportunities, while also providing a platform for diverse views within legal boundaries. Dlamini also indicated the station's intention to hold government accountable by reporting on community service delivery.

sz.headline: Seven Friends Place Bed in Traffic Circle, Face Court
sz.dek: Seven friends pleaded guilty to endangering traffic by placing a bed, pillows, and alcohol in a Mbabane traffic circle for a music video.
paragraphs: Seven friends appeared in Mbabane Magistrate's Court after placing a bed, pillows, and alcohol in the middle of a traffic circle. The group, charged with contravening the Road Traffic Act, admitted to unlawfully endangering themselves and other road users on August 30, 2026, along Somhlolo public road. They were found at the traffic circle with the furniture and drinks, an act that reportedly caused motorists to hoot and attracted police attention.

The accused, Samkeliso Shabangu, Bandile Gama, Siyabonga Ginindza, Lungelo Dlamini, Delisile Shongwe, Lwazi Kunene, and Owethu Lukhozi, stated they were attempting to film a music video to promote their singing careers. During mitigation, they expressed remorse, with some citing a lack of awareness regarding the need for permission and the potential dangers of their actions. Gama mentioned being an unemployed student, while Dlamini explained they were initially waiting for transport for a friend's relocation.

Magistrate Chazile Thwala cautioned the group to research such activities before undertaking them, questioning their judgment in using a bed on a public road. The magistrate remarked on the perceived recklessness of the younger generation. All seven pleaded guilty to the charge, and their apologies and explanations were heard before sentencing.
