ga.headline: Gabon Forum Mobilizes Savings for National Development
ga.dek: The National Savings for Development Forum in Libreville aims to transform national and diaspora savings into long-term financing for economic growth.
paragraphs: Libreville will host the inaugural National Savings for Development Forum (FONED) on September 2 and 3, 2026. Organized by the Caisse des dépôts et consignations du Gabon (CDC Gabon), the event seeks to leverage national and diaspora savings as concrete tools for financing Gabon's development and financial sovereignty. This initiative aligns with the National Growth and Development Plan (PNCD) 2026-2030, which requires twenty-seven thousand billion FCFA in investments, with eighteen thousand billion FCFA expected from the private sector and national resources.

The forum will bring together public authorities, financial institutions, investors, the private sector, experts, and diaspora representatives to discuss transforming savings into long-term financing. Discussions will cover domestic resource mobilization, endogenous financing of the PNCD, productive investment, diaspora savings, and sectors like housing, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, digitalization, and financial inclusion. A study on diaspora savings and development will also be presented.

CDC Gabon aims to solidify its role in mobilizing and securing savings, transforming them into long-term financing and investments aligned with national priorities. The FONED is intended to permanently place savings at the center of national economic debate and foster innovative, sovereign financing models adapted to African development challenges, drawing on continental experiences like that of Morocco's Caisse de Dépôt et Gestion.

ga.headline: Kelly Ondo Obiang Honors Victims, Launches Memoir on Resilience
ga.dek: Ten years after post-election violence, Kelly Ondo Obiang marks the anniversary with a tribute and the release of his autobiographical essay.
paragraphs: Kelly Ondo Obiang paid tribute on August 31, 2026, to victims and families affected by Gabon's 2016 post-election violence, marking the tenth anniversary of the crisis. One year after his release from Libreville Central Prison under an amnesty law, he has dedicated himself to personal reconstruction. He announced the upcoming publication of his autobiographical essay, "L’Espoir doit mourir en dernier" (Hope Must Die Last), which aims to share his experience and reflect on resilience, justice, and rebuilding.

The essay, published by Éditions Filiga, is presented as a method for transforming hardship into leverage and injustice into a demand for change. Ondo Obiang stated, "I am not publishing to recount my pain. I am publishing to offer a method: that of transforming the ordeal into leverage, injustice into demand, and survival into a mission." The book, intended for African youth, seeks to contribute to discussions on overcoming adversity and reclaiming dignity.

The August 31st commemoration also served as a moment for personal reflection, a year after his release. Ondo Obiang described the past twelve months not as a pause but as "labor," dedicated to survival, reconstruction, and regaining his dignity as a citizen. The book's publication is positioned as a contribution to understanding the consequences of adversity and the inner strength required to move forward, even after profound challenges.

ga.headline: Gabon Debt Climbs to 94% of GDP Amidst Ambitious Spending
ga.dek: The International Monetary Fund projects Gabon's public debt to reach 94.3% of GDP by 2027 as infrastructure projects continue.
paragraphs: Gabon's public debt is projected to reach eighty-six point one percent of GDP in 2026 and ninety-four point three percent in 2027, according to the IMF. This surge follows three years of extensive construction across infrastructure sectors, including roads, buildings, and utilities. The nation faces a deficit nearing ten percent of GDP and recently secured a new bond issue of nine hundred twenty million dollars.

The government's initial budget for 2026 proposed significant investment spending, but this was later reduced due to financing realities and project readiness. Investment credits were cut from over three thousand three hundred billion FCFA to around one thousand one hundred sixty-nine billion FCFA in subsequent revisions. This adjustment reflects a recalibration of ambitious initial plans to align with available funding and project maturity.

Despite scaled-back investment figures, Gabon continues to seek capital on international markets. In late July, the country issued bonds worth nine hundred twenty million dollars, maturing in 2033, with an interest rate of nine point three seven five percent. This borrowing comes as the country grapples with financing its development agenda and managing its growing debt burden.

ga.headline: Senate Opens Session, Cites Population Needs
ga.dek: Gabon's Senate convened its second ordinary session, with the chamber's president urging focus on citizens' social and economic expectations.
paragraphs: Gabon's Senate commenced its second ordinary session of the year on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at its temporary headquarters. Presided over by Huguette Yvonne Nyana-Ekoume Awori Onanga, the session's priorities include addressing the social expectations of the populace. The Senate president called for collective, responsible action in service of citizens, highlighting youth, employment, economic diversification, social justice, and good governance as key discussion points.

The Senate president emphasized that numerous expectations remain across various sectors and urged the government to prioritize socio-economic urgencies during the upcoming budget law examination. She stressed the need for particular attention to rehabilitating basic infrastructure, improving living conditions, and ensuring access to essential public services. The session also acknowledged the success of the National Liberation Day celebrations and paid tribute to victims of a recent tragic accident.

During the opening ceremony, attended by the Vice President of the Republic and a regional representative from Mali's Parliament, the Senate president set a tone of focused work and dialogue. She called on senators to evaluate legislation based on its impact on Gabonese citizens and to make the Senate a proactive force for territorial development, emphasizing rigor, openness, and the general interest.

ga.headline: President wears military uniform at liberation celebration
ga.dek: Brice-Clotaire Oligui Nguéma's attire at the 3rd Liberation Day festival raises questions about the separation of military and political power.
paragraphs: President Brice-Clotaire Oligui Nguéma appeared in military uniform, complete with insignia, during the 3rd Liberation Day festival in Makokou. This choice of dress, despite his current role as head of state and supreme commander of defense and security forces, has sparked debate. Although no longer holding a rank within the military hierarchy, his attire evoked his past as a general, leading to discussions about the symbolic representation of power and the distinction between civilian and military institutions.

The president's office had previously stated that an elected president would permanently step down from military service. Nguéma's decision to wear military regalia has prompted interpretations ranging from a tribute to former comrades-in-arms to a potential blurring of lines between the army and politics. This visual choice raises questions about the nature of the post-transition regime and whether the image of a "general-president" should persist.

Separately, a police brigadier named Christian Rodrigue Assogo posted a video pleading for help from President Nguéma and his wife. Assogo, who is paralyzed and suffering from infected wounds, claims his salary and August 17th bonus were cut, leaving him unable to afford medical treatment. He stated that his superiors stopped his pay in July, despite his continued service and deteriorating health.

gm.headline: Caritas-Gambia trains peacebuilders for 2026 elections
gm.dek: The HOPE project equips local leaders and community members with skills to prevent conflict and reduce polarization before the upcoming elections.
paragraphs: Caritas-Gambia has launched a new initiative to foster peace and reduce political polarization ahead of the 2026 elections. The Harmony, Outreach, Peace and Engagement (HOPE) project began training participants yesterday at the Governor's Office in the West Coast Region, with a second phase scheduled for September 3rd in the Lower River Region. National Director Francis D. Mendy stated the project aims to strengthen social cohesion and democratic resilience by empowering youth and women in peacebuilding and electoral processes.

Funded by Catholic Relief Services (CRS), the training focuses on providing practical skills in mediation, dialogue, and early conflict detection. Mendy emphasized the importance of inclusive dialogue between communities and political actors to prevent conflict and help local leaders resolve election-related disputes. The initiative also highlights the crucial role of religious leaders, chiefs, community leaders, youth, women representatives, and civil society organizations in building a peaceful and democratic Gambia.

West Coast Region Deputy Governor Musa Amul Nyassi urged Gambians, especially young people and women, not to be manipulated by politicians into electoral violence. He reminded citizens of their constitutional right to support any party or candidate, stressing that political differences should not disrupt peace and coexistence. Participants are encouraged to apply the acquired knowledge and skills to promote harmony within their communities.

gm.headline: US Visa Curbs Signal Warning to Africa
gm.dek: Washington's tightened immigration policies, citing security and screening concerns, prompt a strategic reevaluation for African nations.
paragraphs: The United States has partially suspended visa issuance for Gambian nationals, affecting visitor, student, exchange, and immigrant visas. This move, attributed by the U.S. administration to security, screening, information sharing, and visa overstay concerns, is viewed not just as an inconvenience but as a strategic warning to the African continent.

Analysts suggest these restrictions can reverberate through international business, medicine, technology, trade, investment, and entrepreneurship. African migrants are integral to a transnational economic ecosystem that links households, companies, universities, and markets across the Atlantic.

The U.S. administration has progressively tightened immigration and visa policies. In January 2026, Washington implemented these partial suspensions, impacting Gambians seeking to visit, study, trade, work, or reunite with family in the United States, subject to specified exceptions.

gm.headline: Brikama Area Council Refinances D58 Million Debt
gm.dek: The council seeks to restructure its outstanding vehicle purchase payments to free up funds for new acquisitions or development projects.
paragraphs: Brikama Area Council (BAC) is proposing to refinance approximately D50 million of its D58 million outstanding debt from a 2024 hire-purchase agreement for waste management vehicles and heavy machinery. The original agreement with Espace Motors was for D101 million, with D43 million already paid, leaving D58 million due in 2026 and 2027. The council aims to secure a new facility from Ecobank, repayable over five years, to manage this obligation.

Chairman Yankuba Darboe stated that this restructuring is intended to release an estimated D20 million in 2026 and D23 million in 2027. These funds could then be allocated to purchasing additional vehicles or supporting other development initiatives within the council's jurisdiction. The council's decision hinges on whether this refinancing offers a better financial outcome compared to the existing payment schedule and other potential financing options.

The move prompts a broader discussion on public institutional finance in The Gambia, questioning when refinancing strengthens an entity and when it merely shifts current liabilities to future budgets. The assessment of BAC's proposed transaction requires a comprehensive analysis of its full financing costs, repayment structure, liquidity impact, associated risks, opportunity costs, asset performance, and implications for future budgets, beyond just the headline figures.

gm.headline: Lawyer Warns Jammeh Return Alliance Tests Gambia Justice
gm.dek: Human rights lawyer Reed Brody stated that any political deal including former dictator Yahya Jammeh's return would challenge the nation's accountability system.
paragraphs: Hungarian-American human rights lawyer Reed Brody has warned that any political alliance aiming to facilitate former dictator Yahya Jammeh's return would severely test Gambia's justice system. Brody stated that such a deal would directly challenge whether accountability can survive electoral politics, especially after years of testimony detailing atrocities. He emphasized that Gambians expect trials, not a negotiated homecoming, and that Jammeh is not above the law.

Brody further clarified that the 2017 Joint Declaration did not guarantee Jammeh safe return and contained no provisions against prosecution, as international law prohibits amnesty for severe crimes. He noted that Gambia has established significant infrastructure for prosecution, including the 2024 Special Accountability Mechanism Act and the December approval of a hybrid Special Tribunal by Ecowas. The naming of Martin Hackett as Special Prosecutor this year marks institutional progress.

Despite institutional advancements, Brody cautioned that justice delivered is not the same as justice on paper. He stressed that the Special Prosecutor's Office requires resources, forensic capacity, and political backing to convert findings into indictments, a process that becomes precarious during an election year. Human activist Madi Jobarteh echoed these concerns, calling any coalition considering Jammeh's return an affront to victims and a threat to national unity.

gn.headline: EDG Union Clashes With Ratoma Commune Over Debt
gn.dek: The electricity union accuses local officials of violence and unpaid bills totaling hundreds of millions of Guinean francs.
paragraphs: Tensions have escalated between the Électricité de Guinée (EDG) union and the Ratoma commune authorities over a disputed debt of hundreds of millions of Guinean francs, the deployment of prepaid meters, and the forceful closure of a local EDG agency. The EDG union claims Ratoma municipality engaged in "intolerable" acts of violence and accumulated "dizzying" payment arrears.

According to Titi Sékou Camara, the union's secretary general, communal agents accompanied by law enforcement allegedly stormed the Taouyah agency last Friday, closing premises, assaulting workers, and leading to hospitalizations. Camara stated the union will file a complaint and suspend electricity supply until payments are made, emphasizing the commune's obligation to install prepaid meters and settle its debt, which he put at over 600 million GNF.

The Ratoma commune, however, disputes the claimed debt amount, calling it "untruths" and asserting that the overall debt attributed to the municipality includes various state sector services. Boubacar Korboyah Baldé, the commune's director of micro-projects, offered a different perspective on the financial obligations.

gn.headline: Guinea Fishery Resumes After Two-Month Ban
gn.dek: Minister Fatima Camara urges sustainable practices as industrial and semi-industrial fishing activities restart within 60 nautical miles.
paragraphs: Industrial and semi-industrial fishing activities officially resumed in Guinea on September 1, 2026, following a two-month biological rest period. The closure, observed from July 1 to August 31, aimed to allow marine species to reproduce and preserve the marine ecosystem. Minister of Fisheries and Maritime Economy, Fatima Camara, called on all sector stakeholders to adhere strictly to sustainable resource management rules upon restarting operations.

The resumption of fishing activities is permitted in the maritime zone extending up to the 60 nautical miles limit, as per the 2026 Maritime Fisheries Management and Planning Plan. During the closure, the government maintained an enhanced surveillance system with collaboration from various maritime services. To mitigate potential shortages and household impacts, authorities had previously authorized duty and tax exemptions for the import of fifteen thousand tons of fishery products.

Minister Camara emphasized that the end of the biological rest does not signify an end to conservation efforts, stressing shared responsibility for preserving and valuing the nation's marine wealth. Scientific assessments of marine stocks are planned to evaluate the impact of the closure and inform future resource management decisions. All actors, including fishmongers, fishermen, shipowners, and economic operators, are urged to exercise rigor and responsibility.

The governor's directive explicitly prohibits any union activities within the BCRG premises, with Dr. Kaba warning that any violations will be met with strict legal consequences. A member of the suspended union delegation confirmed receipt of the notification but declined to comment further on the matter.

This union representative stated that the situation would be managed responsibly and in accordance with the court's decision. The BCRG has informed its staff about the prohibition of union activities and the potential repercussions for non-compliance with the governor's order.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau Votes to Expand Presidential Powers
gw.dek: A referendum proposing a stronger presidential system and a smaller parliament was held Sunday as the military government nears the end of its transition.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau held a referendum Sunday on a new constitution designed to significantly increase presidential authority and reduce the size of parliament. The vote is seen as a key step by the military government to alter the political landscape before scheduled December elections. The proposed changes would shift the country from a semi-presidential to a presidential system, granting the head of state more control over the executive branch, including the power to appoint and dismiss the prime minister.

Under the draft constitution, the president would lead the Council of Ministers, and the number of lawmakers would decrease from 102 to 65, with electoral constituencies reduced from 29 to 12. Supporters of the reforms, including General Tomás Djassi, head of the armed forces, argue these changes will clarify the hierarchy of power and prevent the recurring disputes that have fueled political instability. Critics, however, question the legitimacy of transitional authorities to enact such fundamental constitutional changes.

The opposition, including the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC), has rejected the proposed constitution, urging voters to boycott the referendum. They contend the draft would weaken the prime minister, subordinate parliament and political parties, and excessively concentrate power within the presidency. Concerns have also been raised about the military government's authority to rewrite the constitution during a transitional period.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau Approves Constitutional Overhaul with 70% 'Yes' Vote
gw.dek: A new constitution, strengthening presidential powers and reducing parliamentary seats, passed with broad support across most regions.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau's provisional constitutional referendum results show 70% of voters approved the proposed changes on August 30. The National Elections Commission reported 383,116 "yes" votes against 160,954 "no" votes. Voter turnout was 63%, with 572,712 citizens participating out of 914,428 registered voters, resulting in 37% abstention.

Support for the constitutional revision was strongest in the interior, with Gabú region leading at 90% approval and Bafatá following at 85%. Biombo and Quinara recorded 79% support, while Cacheu and Tombali reached 70%. Oio registered 60% "yes" votes, and Bolama-Bijagós had 58%. Bissau was the sole region to reject the proposal, with 52% voting "no".

Key changes in the new constitution include enhanced presidential authority, a shift from a semi-presidential to a presidential system, and a reduction in the National People's Assembly from 102 to 65 deputies. CNE president Carmem Isaura Tavares Batista Lobo stated the count adhered to the Referendum Law, which deems approved any proposal receiving a majority of affirmative votes.

lr.headline: Evangelical Leader Seeks Deeper Liberia-Israel Business Ties
lr.dek: Association of Evangelicals of Liberia President Bishop Robert Bimba met with the Israeli Ambassador to Ghana to discuss agricultural and educational cooperation.
paragraphs: Bishop Robert Bimba, president of the Association of Evangelicals of Liberia (AEL), has called for enhanced cooperation between Liberia and Israel, focusing on agriculture, education, and faith-based initiatives. This call followed a meeting with Israeli Ambassador to Ghana Roey Gilad in Accra, where discussions explored deepening bilateral relations. Bimba, who also directs the Israel Allies Foundation in Liberia and heads the Community of Hope Agriculture Project, presented a sample of Liberian rice to the ambassador, highlighting the nation's agricultural potential and discussing a proposed dairy farming initiative.

The engagement aimed to leverage faith communities and government efforts to foster development, agricultural transformation, and educational opportunities. Ambassador Gilad encouraged Liberians to utilize available resources and networks for national development. The AEL, representing approximately one million evangelicals in Liberia, also distributed 2,500 solar-powered Gospel lights to pastors and church leaders across the country on August 18.

Bimba appealed to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to consider an official visit to Israel in 2026, citing Liberia's historical support for Israel's establishment at the United Nations. He believes stronger ties could unlock opportunities in agriculture, education, youth development, and religious pilgrimage, utilizing faith-based diplomacy to pursue development goals for Liberia.

lr.headline: Five Liberians Earn UK Chevening Scholarships
lr.dek: Five Liberian scholars will pursue one-year master's degrees in the United Kingdom through the Chevening program.
paragraphs: The British Embassy in Liberia announced five scholars have been selected for the 2026 Chevening Awards, a UK government scholarship program for future leaders. These scholars will travel to the United Kingdom to complete one-year master's degrees at British universities. The program aims to provide fully funded scholarships to individuals who may otherwise find advanced study unaffordable, fostering future leaders in fields such as finance, healthcare, and governance.

The selected scholars and their fields of study are William M. Yarsiah (Special and Inclusive Education at the University of Nottingham), Hawa M. Kamara (Education Studies at Bangor University), Darcess Dossen (Environmental Hazards and Disaster at Cardiff University), Francis M. Bee (Water, Sanitation and Health Engineering at the University of Leeds), and Molley M. Korleh (Port Management at Liverpool John Moores University). The British Embassy congratulated the scholars, wishing them success in their studies and future contributions to Liberia.

Chevening scholarships are designed to equip scholars with academic skills and professional connections, enabling them to become pioneers in their fields and bring back expertise to benefit their home countries. The program boasts a global alumni network of over 50,000, including many prominent figures in politics and business. Chevening has been active in Liberia since 2015, aiming to strengthen ties between the UK and Liberia through educational exchange.

lr.headline: Liberian Students in Rwanda Honor Superintendent Johnson, Receive US$1,200
lr.dek: Grand Bassa County Superintendent Karyou Johnson donated US$1,200 to the Bassa Students Association in Rwanda, recognizing their academic efforts and organization.
paragraphs: The Bassa Students Association in Rwanda (BASIR) honored Grand Bassa County Superintendent Karyou Johnson for his support of their education and welfare. During a gathering, Johnson reaffirmed his commitment to Liberian students abroad and donated US$1,200 towards BASIR’s programs, fulfilling a prior pledge. He encouraged graduating students to return to Liberia and apply their acquired knowledge to national development, emphasizing that education abroad should foster solutions for home.

Superintendent Johnson praised BASIR for its organization, noting their ability to maintain a high level of cooperation without direct sponsorship. He highlighted the achievements of Liberian students in Rwanda as evidence of their potential to positively impact their educational community. Johnson urged graduates to remain resilient in their pursuit of employment and to embrace creativity in leveraging their skills for economic contribution.

Johnson advised students to look beyond traditional job seeking and develop innovative approaches to earning a living and contributing to Liberia’s economy. He shared his own experience transitioning from university to professional life, cautioning that a degree alone does not guarantee employment. The superintendent encouraged graduates to actively seek opportunities and demonstrate the relevance of their foreign education through their work back home.

lr.headline: Robbers Steal Over US$439,000 from Rubber Companies
lr.dek: Unidentified armed men overpowered security at the CRC-MOPP office in Maryland County, making off with cash and documents.
paragraphs: An armed robbery at the shared central office of Cavalla Rubber Corporation (CRC) and MOPP in Pleebo-Sodoken District, Maryland County, has resulted in the loss of over US$439,000, along with Liberian and CFA francs and important company documents. The incident, described as unprecedented, occurred around 3 a.m. when unidentified armed men entered the compound and overpowered security personnel. Three security officers were injured during the attack and are receiving treatment.

The stolen money was intended for the monthly payment of employees of CRC and MOPP. Preliminary information indicates CRC had US$203, L$12,150 and CFA 30,000, while MOPP reportedly had US$235,722, L$270 and CFA 190,000. An ERU officer, Sergeant Romeo Payne, sustained multiple injuries and was disarmed of his weapon, though his M4 rifle was later recovered by authorities.

Two private security officers, Orailey Nance and Moses Dennis, were also injured. The attackers reportedly made off with important company documents in addition to the cash. Authorities are conducting a comprehensive investigation into the early-morning raid, which has disrupted the planned employee payroll for both rubber corporations.

ly.headline: Power cuts cancel children's heart surgeries at Tripoli hospital
ly.dek: Visiting US medical teams and parents face frustration and stress as essential pediatric cardiac procedures are halted due to a lack of reliable electricity and generator fuel.
paragraphs: Open heart surgeries and cardiac catheterization for children were unexpectedly cancelled today at Tripoli University Hospital due to power cuts. Hospital administration could not guarantee a stable power supply, and generators lacked sufficient diesel fuel for uninterrupted operation. The hospital's bypass machine also lacks batteries, further complicating emergency procedures.

The cancellations have left a visiting US medical team, the Novick Cardiac Alliance, frustrated after successfully conducting 18 operations over the past two weeks. The team, from the University of Tennessee Health Science Center's Global Surgical Institute, was scheduled to perform two more critical procedures today alongside Libyan medical staff.

The situation has caused significant distress for parents whose children were awaiting these vital operations. The hospital's inability to maintain consistent power, even with backup generators, highlights critical infrastructure challenges impacting essential medical services for vulnerable young patients.

ly.headline: Dabbashi: '4+4' Agreement is Best Outcome Amid Division
ly.dek: Former UN envoy Ibrahim Dabbashi stated the '4+4 Agreement' is a significant breakthrough for elections, despite divisions among Libyans.
paragraphs: Libya’s former ambassador to the UN, Ibrahim Dabbashi, has described the ‘4+4 Agreement’ as the best possible outcome for overcoming obstacles to elections. He stated on Facebook that the deal, brokered by the UN Support Mission in Libya, represents important progress in the country’s political crisis. Dabbashi noted that while some Libyans oppose the agreement, many citizens are focused on how the country is governed and ending daily hardships rather than specific political figures.

Dabbashi explained that opposition stems from fears of exclusion by certain figures or concerns that the deal extends the power of corrupt officials and delays progress. He characterized the agreement as a compromise that cannot fully satisfy every party, but a major breakthrough in overcoming barriers to presidential and parliamentary elections. He believes the deal is the best the UN could achieve given deep stakeholder divisions and foreign interference.

The former ambassador warned that the current situation could persist for years or lead to war, emphasizing that no alternative exists to change the ground reality or compel parties to relinquish control. Dabbashi urged societal unity and peaceful pressure for the agreement's implementation, advocating for unified authorities composed of capable, honest, and professional figures to build accountable institutions and restore state dignity.

ly.headline: Libya Electricity Grid Suffers Partial Blackout
ly.dek: Western Libya experienced a partial power outage in the early hours of this morning, despite recent assurances from the General Electricity Company of Libya.
paragraphs: The General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL) announced a partial blackout affecting the western section of the electrical grid early today. This incident follows recent assurances from GECOL management that the worst of the country's power cuts were over, with a new power station nearing operation and peak summer demand expected to subside.

GECOL stated the outage occurred after a disturbance caused two major transmission circuits, Misrata/Al-Khoms 400kV and Bir Al-Ghanam/Al-Ruwais, to trip. This led to a significant frequency drop from 50 Hz to 47.5 Hz, indicating a loss of balance between electricity generation and demand. The company is investigating whether the cause was technical faults or deliberate sabotage.

A thorough technical investigation into the protection system logs is underway to determine the exact cause of the circuit trips. GECOL has pledged to restore system stability and will transparently disclose the findings to pursue legal measures against any interference with these vital national security assets.

mg.headline: Ravalomanana sentenced to ten years for 2025 protest violence
mg.dek: The former Senate president was convicted of complicity in murder and intentional injury related to the repression of demonstrations in Antananarivo.
paragraphs: Former Senate president General Richard Ravalomanana has been sentenced to ten years of forced labor for his role in violence during September and October 2025 protests in Antananarivo. The court found him guilty of complicity in murder and intentional injury, alleging he instructed security forces to use violence and facilitated abuses against demonstrators. The case included accusations of dragging a person and gendarmes burning protesters' hair, though Ravalomanana denied any involvement.

The defense argued that no direct evidence, such as written or verbal orders, linked Ravalomanana to the violence, and that he was not part of the operational chain of command. An earlier charge of threatening a former director of Sirama was dismissed due to prescription and the complainant withdrawing his complaint. Despite the defense's arguments, the court convicted the former Senate president, who is to be imprisoned at Imerintsiatosika high-security prison.

Ravalomanana's lawyer has announced an appeal to the Court of Cassation, seeking to overturn the verdict. The conviction stems from events between September 25 and October 11, 2025, where authorities responded to demonstrations. The prosecution's case focused on Ravalomanana's alleged instructions to security forces, which he and a former national police director denied, stating operations were managed by structures under the Prime Minister and a mixed operational staff.

mg.headline: Madagascar Airlines grounds ATR plane due to engine shortage
mg.dek: The national carrier faces continued flight disruptions as two essential reserve engines undergo maintenance in Europe.
paragraphs: Madagascar Airlines is experiencing ongoing flight disruptions because two reserve engines for one of its five ATR aircraft are delayed in delivery. These engines are undergoing regulatory maintenance in European workshops. The airline's management stated yesterday that they are awaiting the engines' return after multiple postponements.

The delivery was initially scheduled for August 27, then moved to September 2, but has been delayed again. The airline's director general, Rado Rabarilala, indicated a further one-week delay is expected without a precise new date. French and German embassies have intervened to expedite repairs.

With only four aircraft now operational, Madagascar Airlines must adjust flight schedules, impacting regularity and punctuality. The company apologizes for the inconvenience and is covering hotel costs for affected passengers. The director general acknowledged a lack of specific delivery timelines in the contract, noting engine maintenance can exceed two million dollars, of which approximately 375,000 dollars remain outstanding.

mg.headline: Magistrates Union Challenges Justice Ministry Over Suspensions
mg.dek: The Magistrates Union of Madagascar contests the Justice Ministry's handling of three anti-corruption magistrates' suspensions, escalating a dispute over disciplinary procedures.
paragraphs: The Magistrates Union of Madagascar (SMM) has publicly challenged the Ministry of Justice regarding the suspension of three magistrates from the Anti-Corruption Pole (PAC) in Antananarivo. SMM President Mbintanarivo Andriantsihorisoa stated that the magistrates should have been informed of the specific grievances against them and allowed to present their defense before any action was taken. The union alleges this constitutes "harassment" and that their request for a prior review of the situation was ignored.

The SMM is also raising broader concerns about directives issued to magistrates on sensitive cases, demanding that any instructions influencing decisions or legal interpretations be formalized in writing. This demand directly addresses concerns about judicial independence and protection from hierarchical pressure. The union is not limiting its response to public protest and is seeking the suspension of the measure against the three magistrates, initiating a new conflict with the Ministry.

The Ministry of Justice justified the sanctions by citing alleged failures in case management and professional responsibilities, following an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Pole Monitoring and Evaluation Committee. The ministry affirmed its commitment to strictly applying regulations without differential treatment. This opposition presents two conflicting views: the Ministry emphasizes professional accountability and adherence to rules, while the SMM criticizes the procedure and defends the sanctioned magistrates, signaling a wider institutional confrontation.

mg.headline: New Rice Variety 'Besalohy' Promises 6 Tons Per Hectare
mg.dek: Developed through collaboration, the Besalohy rice variety offers high yields and adaptability to various Malagasy soil conditions.
paragraphs: Madagascar's agriculture sector sees a significant advancement with the introduction of the new rice variety, 'Besalohy'. This development is the result of a partnership between the Research Center for Rural Development (Fofifa) and the Japan International Research Center for Agricultural Sciences (Jircas). The variety is noted for its quality, distinct appearance, and aroma, and is suitable for local climate conditions.

Besalohy rice contributes to productive and sustainable rice cultivation, particularly in less fertile lands. It can yield up to six tons per hectare and can be planted in any season. Fofifa and Jircas conducted research and trials from 2021 in locations including Kianjasoa, Itasy, and Toamasina, with successful outcomes.

The development of Besalohy utilized molecular techniques to improve rice varieties, ensuring good yields even in challenging or infertile soils. The variety has a life cycle of approximately three months and its seeds can be reused. Fofifa's Director General, Pr Jean Michel Leong Pock Tsy, stated the goal is to continuously improve yields by listening to farmers' needs and observing current conditions.

mg.headline: Madagascar Sees Spike in Fire Alerts
mg.dek: Satellite data reveals 17,485 fire alerts between August 2025 and August 2026, an exceptionally high number compared to previous years.
paragraphs: Madagascar is experiencing its peak season for bush and forest fires, a period that typically lasts seventeen weeks. Between August 18, 2025, and August 24, 2026, a total of 17,485 fire alert points were recorded across the country. This figure, derived from reliable data from VIIRS and Global Forest Watch, is noted as exceptionally high when compared to previous years, reaching back to 2012.

The platform also indicates that from 2001 to 2025, Madagascar lost 350,000 hectares of forest due to fires, with the year 2014 marking the largest loss of forest cover during the high season, at 49,000 hectares destroyed. In response to this trend, Madagascar National Parks (MNP) has begun distributing protective equipment to its field agents as part of its fire management strategy.

This initiative, conducted in partnership with the French association Baroudeur Massilia Pompiers du Monde, aligns with national policies for disaster risk management. Eighty-three individual protective equipment kits were distributed across eleven Madagascar National Parks sites, supporting the national contingency plan for bush and forest fires signed in December 2024.

mw.headline: Malawi Aviation Deficiencies Revealed After Vice President's Plane Crash
mw.dek: A parliamentary inquiry heard testimony that Malawi's aviation infrastructure suffers from long-standing structural deficiencies, risking failure in an upcoming international.
paragraphs: An inquiry into the June 10, 2024 plane crash that killed Vice-President Saulos Chilima and eight others has revealed significant structural deficiencies in Malawi's aviation infrastructure. Fredrick Chisepeya, director of Aerodromes and Air Navigation Standards at the Civil Aviation Authority of Malawi, told a parliamentary committee that the country risks failing an upcoming International Civil Aviation Organisation audit unless urgent investment is made in safety and security.

Testimony indicated that Malawi possesses only one secondary flight surveillance radar, located at Kamuzu International Airport, which has diminished coverage at lower altitudes. This gap meant the aircraft carrying the Vice-President was outside radar coverage when it crashed. Furthermore, Mzuzu Airport, the intended destination, operated at a safety level of three on a ten-point scale, well below the required six for medium-sized aircraft, with deficiencies in fire response and runway conditions.

Compounding these issues, Mzuzu Airport was operating without a valid license at the time of the crash, only receiving one in 2025 with attached conditions. The Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services also stated that no airport weather forecaster was deployed to Mzuzu Airport on the day of the flight, as the department was unaware of the planned flight due to Mzuzu Airport not receiving commercial flights at the time. Mandatory weather forecast checks were not conducted for the flight.

mw.headline: Alliance Demands Increased Investment for Non-Communicable Disease Care
mw.dek: The Non-Communicable Diseases Alliance Malawi is calling for sustained funding and improved services to address the growing burden of diseases like cancer and diabetes.
paragraphs: The Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Alliance Malawi has urged for continuous investment in essential services to enhance treatment access for NCDs across the country. This call comes ahead of the Global Week for Action on NCDs 2026, an event focused on tangible improvements in healthcare delivery. NCDs, encompassing conditions such as cardiovascular diseases, cancers, diabetes, and chronic respiratory illnesses, are responsible for approximately 40 percent of all deaths in Malawi.

The alliance specifically requested accelerated action to ensure World Health Organization (WHO) PEN and PEN-Plus strategies are well-resourced, functional, and accessible, particularly in rural areas. These WHO strategies aim to manage NCDs in low-resource settings. The call emphasizes the need for investment in healthcare workers, medicines, diagnostics, screening, referral systems, and health information systems, alongside efforts to reduce risk factors like tobacco use, unhealthy diets, and inactivity.

Public health advocate Maziko Matemba stated that the Global Week for Action serves as a vital platform to move from political promises to active healthcare delivery. The event aims to bridge global commitments with local realities, seeking more consistent access to affordable medicines, reliable diagnostic tools, and comprehensive care networks. Participants will endorse the Malawi GW4A NCD Charter 2026, which will be presented to the Parliamentary Committee on Health to advocate for stronger political leadership and accountability in addressing NCDs.

mw.headline: Ministry Awaits Funding for Bingu Stadium Fence Repairs
mw.dek: Security lapses at Bingu National Stadium persist due to unaddressed perimeter fence vulnerabilities, as the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Culture seeks funding for repairs.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Youth, Sports and Culture has acknowledged ongoing security issues at Bingu National Stadium, citing a lack of funding to repair the perimeter fence. Gaping holes in the fence have allowed fans to enter the venue without tickets, contributing to poor gate management. The ministry has proposed building a brick fence in vulnerable sections to address these security gaps.

These security concerns were highlighted during the recent Airtel Top 8 final between Mighty Wanderers and Ekhaya, which generated K87 million in gate revenue. Despite the presence of security personnel, some fans gained unauthorized entry by exploiting weak points in the fence. Long queues and a mismatch between ticket sales and available security staff exacerbated the problem, making it easier for gatecrashers to slip through.

The stadium is scheduled to host a Caf Champions League match between Mighty Wanderers and Simba SC this Sunday, adding urgency to the security situation. Mighty Wanderers has pledged to implement enhanced security measures for the upcoming continental fixture. The ministry continues to await funding to implement the proposed fence repairs and address the stadium's security vulnerabilities.

mw.headline: Power outages disrupt Rumphi Hospital services
mw.dek: Frequent blackouts at the district's referral hospital are impacting patient care and health worker operations.
paragraphs: Patients at Rumphi District Hospital are experiencing disruptions to essential health services due to persistent power blackouts. The district's key referral facility lacks a reliable backup power system, leading to prolonged electricity interruptions that negatively affect operations and patient care. Health workers face significant challenges as the entire hospital is plunged into darkness when the national power grid fails, hindering their ability to perform duties and potentially risking patient lives.

The absence of a dependable alternative electricity source means hospital operations are severely impacted by national grid failures. These disruptions affect critical services requiring continuous power, including patient care, lighting, medical equipment operation, and laboratory services. The Rumphi District Council is considering engaging local Members of Parliament to find solutions for a dependable backup power supply.

Concerns are mounting over the hospital's vulnerability to power outages, with civil society groups urging the council to prioritize installing a reliable backup system. Such an investment is crucial to protect patients, support health workers, and ensure vital services remain operational. Reliable electricity is essential for adequate lighting, operating medical equipment, preserving medicines, and ensuring safe patient care, especially during emergencies and at night.

ml.headline: Mali Media Sector Reforms Launch Two New Oversight Bodies
ml.dek: Two new structures, a collective bargaining agreement review commission and a media self-regulation body, aim to modernize Mali's journalism profession.
paragraphs: Mali's media sector is undergoing reform with the establishment of two new entities. The Maison de la presse officially launched a commission on August 28 to revise the journalists' collective bargaining agreement and a preparatory committee for a future media self-regulation body, the CPOAM. These initiatives are intended to align regulations with current realities, improve working conditions, and enhance professional accountability.

The collective bargaining agreement review will consider the perspectives of both media owners and journalists, aiming for better implementation of existing provisions and clearer responsibility in cases of misconduct. Journalists like Kadiatou Sanogo of Maliweb anticipate improved working conditions and greater professional responsibility. Mahamadou Touré of Le Guido sees the reforms as crucial for protecting journalists' rights, particularly for younger professionals facing difficult conditions and low pay, noting that the sector "no longer feeds its man."

The creation of the CPOAM, a future media self-regulation organ, runs parallel to the collective agreement review. This move signals a broader effort to professionalize journalism in Mali. The reforms are expected to address issues ranging from fair wages to ethical conduct, aiming to strengthen the profession's integrity and sustainability in the face of current challenges.

ml.headline: Mali Leads African Consortium Developing Single-Dose Malaria Treatment
ml.dek: Eleven African and European partners are collaborating on a new antimalarial drug to combat growing resistance to existing treatments.
paragraphs: Mali is spearheading WANECAM3, an international consortium focused on creating a revolutionary single-dose malaria treatment. This initiative, based at the University of Science, Techniques and Technologies in Bamako, involves eleven partners from six African nations and four European countries. The project aims to develop the next generation of malaria therapies to address the increasing resistance to current drugs, particularly artemisinin derivatives, which have been crucial in saving millions of lives.

The research is co-financed by the European Union through Global Health EDCTP3 and private entities like Novartis and Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV). WANECAM3 is concentrating on entirely new antimalarial compounds, distinct from artemisinin derivatives. Phase 2 and 3 clinical trials will evaluate these molecules on patients in real African settings, with the ultimate goal of achieving a curative, single-dose treatment for uncomplicated malaria.

This scientific endeavor represents a significant geopolitical and economic opportunity. While the European Union seeks access to African medical innovations, companies like Novartis and MMV see a multi-billion dollar market in Africa and Southeast Asia. For Mali, the project offers a chance to gain scientific and medical sovereignty, moving from importing solutions to creating them, though questions remain about patent control and affordable access for African patients.

ml.headline: Malian Army Strikes Terrorist Camps Near Aguelhoc, Kignan, Niono
ml.dek: Malian armed forces reported successful strikes on multiple terrorist gathering points across the country on August 30 and 31, 2026.
paragraphs: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by partners, conducted significant operations against armed groups on August 30 and 31, 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. Intelligence led to successful strikes on identified terrorist regrouping points west of Aguelhoc, which contained war materials. On the same day, FAMa targeted a terrorist position west of Kignan following pursuit operations.

Further operations on August 31, 2026, involved surveillance near Niono, where multiple terrorist gathering points with observed war materials were identified and struck north-west of the city. Surveillance and reconnaissance are ongoing in these areas to assess the full impact and neutralize any remaining threats.

The Malian General Staff reaffirmed the armed forces' commitment to rigorous and professional security operations nationwide. Separately, the village of Ningari in the Bandiagara region was attacked on August 31, 2026, with shops looted and animals taken, prompting a local call for a permanent security presence.

ml.headline: Explosion Kills Five in Gao Neighborhood
ml.dek: An explosion in Gao's Anoura neighborhood killed five people and injured two, raising concerns about unexploded ordnance.
paragraphs: Five people died and two were seriously injured on Saturday, August 29, in the Anoura neighborhood of Gao. Local sources cited by Studio Tamani suggest the victims were handling an unexploded shell, though this remains unconfirmed by official investigation. The incident occurred away from reported military clashes in the area, and the exact nature, origin, and circumstances of the explosive device are not yet public.

The powerful explosion, capable of causing such fatalities, occurred in an inhabited space, highlighting the risk of explosive remnants of war. Specialists are needed to examine the site, identify fragments, and determine if this was an isolated accident or indicative of wider contamination. Understanding the object's history, from discovery to potential circulation, is crucial to prevent future tragedies.

The incident underscores the persistent danger of explosive devices in Mali, where 268 victims, including 119 deaths, were recorded in 2024 from mines and explosive remnants. Metal scavenging, a livelihood for some, can lead to accidental contact with altered military items. Residents are urged to leave any suspected ordnance untouched and report it to authorities.

ml.headline: Mali Government Distributes Over 200 Tonnes of Millet
ml.dek: Food aid arrives in Bankass commune to support vulnerable populations facing hardship during the lean season.
paragraphs: The Malian government has begun distributing over 200 tonnes of millet across several communes in the Bankass district. The operation, part of a governmental solidarity initiative during the lean season, commenced on Monday, August 31, in Bankass commune. This distribution aims to provide essential food support to vulnerable residents experiencing difficulties.

Specific allocations include 74 tonnes of millet for Bankass, 57 tonnes for Diallassagou, and 38 tonnes each for Lessagou and Koulogon. The initiative is designed to alleviate food insecurity for those most affected by the current period of scarcity, ensuring access to vital grain supplies.

This delivery of food supplies is a direct response to the challenges posed by the 'soudure,' or lean season, a critical time when food reserves are typically low. The government's intervention seeks to bridge this gap and prevent widespread hunger among the population.

mr.headline: Global Transparency Finds Faulty Cables in Nouakchott Power Station Fires
mr.dek: An investigation by Global Transparency points to non-compliant cables and a company linked to a parliamentarian as potential causes for recent electrical fires.
paragraphs: An investigation by the organization Global Transparency has identified technical suspicions and a potential conflict of interest in the recent fires at two Nouakchott electrical substations. The organization focused on cables supplied and installed by CTM Bâtiment, a company reportedly owned by a local parliamentarian, examining their conformity to project specifications and the circumstances of their installation. Technical sources indicated that newly installed cables showed problems and were disconnected as a precaution before the fires occurred.

The report suggests that non-compliant cables or installation errors could be contributing factors, citing video evidence reviewed by a Somelec official. This evidence indicated that smoke originated from recently connected new cables. Global Transparency dismissed sabotage and grid overload as primary causes, noting that one of the burned substations was not connected to a line implicated in overload theories.

The organization also questioned CTM Bâtiment's experience, as the tender required prior completion of two medium-voltage substation projects. While CTM Bâtiment listed a solar power project in Zoueirat on its website as a completed EPC project, a SNIM report indicated CTM Bâtiment handled only construction, with BGL Energy managing technical installations.

mr.headline: Health Ministry Prepares 28 New Health Centers for Nouakchott
mr.dek: Minister Thiam Tidjani chaired a meeting to finalize preparations for 28 new health facilities in the capital, assessing needs for staff and equipment.
paragraphs: The Mauritanian Ministry of Health is in the final stages of preparing 28 new health centers for service in Nouakchott. These facilities are part of an emergency program aimed at developing the capital city. Minister Thiam Tidjani recently led a meeting with regional health directors and chief physicians from Nouakchott's three wilayas to review the readiness of these centers.

The meeting focused on identifying the specific requirements for each center, including the necessary number of doctors, nurses, and other health personnel. Discussions also covered the installation of equipment and the establishment of a system for distributing human resources to ensure a smooth launch of services. The minister stressed the importance of coordination between central and regional administrations.

The health component of Nouakchott's emergency development program includes 28 health establishments across the capital's nine districts. These involve new constructions, equipment procurement, and rehabilitation of existing facilities. The goal is to ensure these centers are fully operational and ready to serve citizens upon opening.

mr.headline: Opposition Party Denounces Rights Violations, Warns of Consequences
mr.dek: The Union of Progress Forces party criticizes the use of courts to suppress free speech and opposes constitutional changes for a third presidential term.
paragraphs: The opposition party Union of Progress Forces has warned of a "climate of violation of liberties," stating that using the justice system to stifle free expression and deter those who report abuses could severely impact public freedoms. This declaration followed a regular session of the party's executive bureau, where national, regional, and international situations, along with political and organizational matters, were discussed.

The party also condemned calls to amend the constitution to allow a third presidential term. They view this as a threat to stability and an attempt to negatively influence upcoming dialogue. The executive bureau approved plans to hold a party congress after the upcoming Ramadan, with an extraordinary session scheduled for late December to prepare for it.

The Union of Progress Forces' statement highlights concerns over the erosion of democratic space and potential political instability stemming from attempts to extend presidential terms. The party's leadership is preparing for internal organizational changes, including a congress to be held after Ramadan.

mr.headline: Mauritania Caps Financial Transfer Tax at 200 Ouguiyas
mr.dek: The tax on financial transfers will not exceed 200 new ouguiyas, regardless of the transfer amount, effective September 1.
paragraphs: Mauritania's General Tax Administration has set a new maximum of 200 new ouguiyas for taxes on financial transfers. This measure, which applies to all banks operating in the country, aims to cap the tax amount irrespective of the sum being transferred. The new regulation is scheduled to take effect no later than September 1.

The tax will be calculated at 0.1% of the transfer's value, with the 200 new ouguiyas ceiling in place. Mokhtar Salem El-Mouna, the Director General of Taxes, met with bank representatives to instruct them to implement the necessary technical and administrative adjustments to their systems to ensure uniform application of the new rules.

Bank representatives have committed to adopting the required measures and beginning the application of the capped tax on financial transfers by the September 1 deadline. The General Tax Administration confirmed this commitment, signaling a shift in how financial transactions will be taxed across the nation.

mr.headline: Mauritanian Minister Links Peace to Structural Causes of Conflict
mr.dek: Minister Hanena Ould Sidi stated that addressing poverty, unemployment, and weak governance is essential for lasting peace in Africa.
paragraphs: Mauritanian Defense Minister Hanena Ould Sidi asserted that achieving peace in Africa requires tackling the root causes of conflict, including institutional fragility, poverty, unemployment, poor governance, social inequality, and limited opportunities for youth. Speaking at the African Union summit in Luanda, he emphasized that establishing the rule of law, strengthening justice, and fostering national cohesion are crucial for continental security.

Ould Sidi highlighted Mauritania's "integrated security approach," which posits that sustainable development is impossible without security, and vice versa, especially when institutional, economic, and social fragility prevails. The summit focused on enhancing conflict prevention and resolution mechanisms, developing AU political and legal tools, and supporting mediation efforts.

Discussions also centered on promoting "African solutions to African problems" and mobilizing resources for stability and development. The Mauritanian delegation included Ambassador Mohamed Ould Mekhalla and Ambassador El-Houssein Ould Naji, among other officials.

mu.headline: Prime Minister Contradicts Health Minister's Surgery Account
mu.dek: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam stated the surgery was performed by a private practitioner, contradicting his Health Minister's earlier claims.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam directly contradicted Health Minister Anil Bachoo's account of his recent surgery at Dr. A. G. Jeetoo Hospital. Responding to the opposition leader in Parliament, Ramgoolam stated that the operation was performed by a private practitioner, Dr. Sookha, not the public hospital's surgeon as Bachoo had asserted for ten days. Bachoo had previously claimed his private doctor was merely an observer and that the procedure was standard practice.

The Prime Minister's statement implies Minister Bachoo was unaware of who performed his surgery, as Ramgoolam suggested Bachoo was under anesthesia and thus unable to know the details. This explanation has been met with skepticism, as it suggests Bachoo confidently provided a version of events he could not have personally verified. The contradiction has fueled controversy and calls for clarification on the authorization and public resources used.

The government is now considering a protocol to allow public access to similar arrangements in the future. This announcement raises questions about the legitimacy of the Health Minister's procedure, given that a protocol for such interventions did not exist at the time. The situation has led to accusations that Minister Bachoo misled the public regarding his surgery.

mu.headline: Mauritius Reassesses Drug War Metrics Amid Rising Arrests
mu.dek: The nation's drug control strategy now emphasizes reducing harm and demand over solely focusing on enforcement statistics.
paragraphs: Mauritius is shifting its approach to the drug problem, moving beyond a simple measure of success based on arrests and seizures. The National Drug Control Master Plan 2026–2030 introduces a four-pillar strategy: reducing drug supply and demand, improving health and wellbeing, and fostering a coordinated national response. This plan acknowledges that drugs present multifaceted challenges across criminal justice, public health, social, economic, and governance sectors.

In 2024, authorities recorded 4,373 drug-related infractions and made 2,520 arrests, according to data from the National Drug Observatory. While these figures indicate significant enforcement activity, they do not necessarily reflect a reduction in drug use or associated harms. The policy shift aims to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions by measuring tangible outcomes rather than just enforcement actions.

The new framework seeks to answer more complex questions, such as whether drug dependency is decreasing, if major trafficking networks are being dismantled, and if drug-related hospital admissions and deaths are declining. The focus is on achieving measurable reductions in drug-related harm and improving community safety through a comprehensive and coordinated national effort.

mu.headline: Absa Warns Customers of Fake Mobile Banking App Scams
mu.dek: Absa Mauritius is alerting clients to fraudulent Facebook pages and websites promoting a non-existent mobile banking application.
paragraphs: Absa Mauritius has issued a warning to its customers regarding fake Facebook pages and websites that are falsely advertising a new mobile banking application. The bank has clarified that it has not launched any new application through these channels, urging clients to be vigilant.

Fraudsters are reportedly using advertisements and messages to trick users into clicking malicious links or divulging personal information. Absa advises customers to only download applications from official platforms and to never share passwords, PINs, or one-time passwords. The bank also stressed the importance of being wary of suspicious links.

This alert aims to protect customers from potential financial fraud and identity theft. By emphasizing the use of official app stores and secure practices, Absa seeks to prevent clients from falling victim to these deceptive online tactics.

mu.headline: Wife Recovers Vehicle Seized in Drug Trafficking Probe
mu.dek: Véronique Leu-Govind's GWM Tank 300 was returned after police approved a request from her lawyer.
paragraphs: Véronique Leu-Govind has regained possession of her GWM Tank 300 all-terrain vehicle. The keys were handed over on Tuesday morning, September 1, 2026, at the Western Division police headquarters. This restitution follows a formal request made by her lawyer, Me Shafick Chuttur, to the police and the Director of Public Prosecutions office. The vehicle had been seized by the ADSU of Rose-Hill on July 30 as part of an investigation into alleged zamal trafficking between La Réunion and Mauritius.

The operation that led to the vehicle's seizure also resulted in the arrest of Leu-Govind's husband, Gulshan Govind. Police investigations at the time focused on the discovery of a methadone vial and cannabis at their home, and Govind's potential involvement in drug trafficking. The GWM Tank 300 underwent examination by Scene of Crime Office experts before its return to Leu-Govind.

Gulshan Govind remains in provisional detention. His next court appearance is scheduled for September 7, 2026, at 1 p.m. before the Bambous tribunal. The investigation into the alleged zamal trafficking continues, with authorities examining the extent of the operation and any connections between La Réunion and Mauritius.

mz.headline: Mondlane Trial Puts Government in Political Bind
mz.dek: A conviction could silence Mozambique's leading opposition figure, but the trial may also amplify his message and expose government actions.
paragraphs: Venâncio Mondlane's trial presents Mozambique's government with a difficult political choice. A conviction could sideline the country's most effective opposition politician, but the proceedings might also provide Mondlane with a national stage to criticize the disputed 2024 elections and government actions.

Both Mondlane and his legal team have requested the trial be broadcast live, viewing it as an opportunity to scrutinize the election process, police conduct, and the government's treatment of opponents. The charges, including "incitement to terrorism," carry potential sentences exceeding twenty years, raising questions about the necessity of Council of State authorization for proceedings.

The Supreme Court faces a test in impartially assessing this politically charged case, requiring the prosecution to prove each charge with evidence. The post-election unrest stemmed from widespread frustration over election results and the state's response, not solely from Mondlane's calls for demonstrations.

mz.headline: Malnutrition Kills Children in Nampula Province
mz.dek: Thirteen children died from acute malnutrition in the first six months of the year in Nampula.
paragraphs: Acute malnutrition continues to claim lives in Nampula province. In the first six months of the year, thirteen children died from the condition, out of more than sixteen thousand diagnosed. Poor nutrition is identified as the underlying cause of these deaths.

The pediatric ward at the Central Hospital of Nampula frequently experiences overcrowding during peak periods, indicating a significant burden of cases. The consistent rise in malnutrition diagnoses points to ongoing challenges in ensuring adequate nutrient intake for the province's youngest residents.

The situation highlights a persistent public health crisis in the region, with the number of affected children underscoring the scale of the problem. Efforts to address the root causes of poor nutrition are crucial to reducing child mortality in Nampula.

mz.headline: President Revokes Central Bank Governor Appointment
mz.dek: Waldemar de Sousa's appointment as governor of the Bank of Mozambique was revoked less than 24 hours after being named, following public concerns.
paragraphs: President Daniel Chapo revoked the appointment of Waldemar de Sousa as governor of the Bank of Mozambique today, reversing a decision made less than a day prior. The Presidency cited "supervening issues" for the reversal, but did not confirm if it was related to a reported 2020 criminal case concerning administrative authorisations linked to hidden debts. Activist Adriano Nuvunga publicly raised the case shortly before the appointment was revoked, leading to public speculation.

The timing of the revocation, coupled with the public resurfacing of the 2020 case, invites the conclusion that the criminal investigation was the cause. However, this remains an inference as the Presidency has not officially confirmed it. The accusation was reportedly public knowledge six years prior, raising questions about the vetting process for high-level state appointments and the role of security services in reviewing potential appointees' records.

If the security services vetted Sousa, they should have identified the unresolved case and reported it, making the subsequent appointment questionable. Conversely, if they failed to discover information readily available in the public record, it indicates a serious lapse in their due diligence. This situation raises concerns about the integrity checks applied to presidential appointments, particularly for sensitive positions like the central bank governor.

mz.headline: Anamola Demands Fair Trial for Leader Venâncio Mondlane
mz.dek: The National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique calls for an independent and transparent judicial process for its leader facing five criminal charges.
paragraphs: Anamola is demanding an independent, impartial, and transparent trial for its leader, former presidential candidate Venâncio Mondlane. The Supreme Court of Mozambique has summoned Mondlane to face five criminal charges stemming from post-election protests. The demonstrations, called by Mondlane to contest alleged fraud in the October 2024 general elections, began peacefully but escalated into riots. Mondlane is accused of public incitement to crime, collective disobedience, and terrorism-related offenses.

The Council of State, an advisory body to the Mozambican President, recently decided to lift Mondlane's parliamentary immunity to allow his trial. Mondlane holds a seat on the Council of State due to his position as the runner-up in the last presidential election. Anamola spokesperson Manuela Veloso stated that the trial must strictly adhere to the Constitution and national laws, emphasizing that respect for institutions does not equate to blind trust and defending peace should not mean accepting injustice.

Anamola rejects claims that Mondlane incited violence, attributing the unrest to police actions. According to the NGO "Decide" Platform, police fatally shot approximately 400 people and injured 619 during five months of disturbances starting October 21, 2024. While the Attorney General's Office initiated 31 legal cases against police officers, no convictions have been secured. Anamola also requested the trial be broadcast live on television and social media.

mz.headline: EU Names New Ambassador to Mozambique
mz.dek: Francisco Fontán Pardo assumes the role with a focus on cooperation, peace, and stability.
paragraphs: The European Union has appointed Francisco Fontán Pardo as its new ambassador to Mozambique, succeeding Antonino Maggiore. Pardo officially takes up his post on Tuesday, with his mandate prioritizing the consolidation of cooperation and efforts to maintain peace in the country. The appointment was made by the EU's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, Kaja Kallas.

In his new role, Pardo has pledged to make peace and the development of Mozambique key priorities. He stated his commitment to strengthening the relationship between the EU and Mozambique, advancing common goals for sustainable development, peace consolidation, stability, and shared prosperity. Pardo will present his credentials to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation in the coming days.

Pardo brings extensive diplomatic experience from the European External Action Service, having previously served as Deputy Head of the EU Delegation in Brazil and Chief of Staff for a former High Representative. He also served as the EU Ambassador to ASEAN. The EU has been a significant international partner for Mozambique, supporting its security, economic development, and institutional strengthening.

na.headline: Venaani Demands Factory Plan Funding Details
na.dek: Opposition leader McHenry Venaani questioned the government's undisclosed plans for regional manufacturing facilities and their funding sources.
paragraphs: Popular Democratic Movement president McHenry Venaani is demanding clarity on the government's strategy to establish manufacturing and processing facilities across all 14 Namibian regions. He questioned how the program will be funded, implemented, and utilized for job creation during a National Assembly session. While welcoming the initiative's goals of promoting local value addition, economic diversification, and job creation, Venaani stated that project specifics have not been publicly disclosed.

Venaani specifically asked for details on identified manufacturing and processing projects, their locations, and the estimated total investment required, including contributions from the government, private sector, and other investors. A key concern is whether the private sector will lead ownership and operation, rather than creating government-dependent enterprises. He also requested implementation timelines, including construction start dates, operational readiness, and job creation projections.

The questions arise as the government reports progress on expanding manufacturing beyond main economic centers. Venaani seeks information on expected direct and indirect job creation, methods for measuring employment targets, and how local farmers, entrepreneurs, small and medium-sized enterprises, and manufacturers will be integrated into supply chains. This pushes the government for concrete details beyond broad policy statements on projects, funding, timelines, and jobs.

na.headline: Robben Island Prisoner Helao Shityuwete Dies at 92
na.dek: Former anti-apartheid activist Helao Shityuwete, who spent 18 years imprisoned on Robben Island, died at 92 in Windhoek.
paragraphs: Helao Shityuwete, a former Robben Island political prisoner and anti-apartheid activist, has died at the age of 92. Shityuwete passed away on Saturday in Windhoek. He was imprisoned for 18 years on Robben Island for his role in Namibia’s liberation struggle. He was described by his daughter, Tulimelila Shityuwete, as a principled, warm, gentle, and kind individual who was also a very involved father.

Shityuwete was a strong advocate for workers' rights and dignity in Namibia. He founded the Namibian Former Robben Island Prisoners Trust to support former prisoners and their families, addressing the poverty many faced after release. His wife, Jane, recalled meeting him in London in 1986 and described him as a handsome, tall, and charismatic man. Shityuwete's death leaves Betuel Nuunyango as the sole surviving member of the 37 Namibian nationalists incarcerated on Robben Island in the 1960s.

Born in Angola, Shityuwete moved to Namibia at age 10 and was educated at Endola and St Mary's Mission in Odibo. In 1967, he and 36 others were tried under South Africa's Terrorism Act, convicted, and sent to Robben Island in 1968, with Shityuwete being released in 1984. Vicky ya Toivo, widow of Andimba Toivo ya Toivo, remembered Shityuwete as a beautiful soul, a reader, and a leader with whom their families shared warmth and cohesion.

na.headline: Namibia Cabinet Clarifies Mining Rules for Sensitive Areas
na.dek: New policy framework aims to balance economic benefits with strict environmental standards for resource extraction.
paragraphs: Namibia's Cabinet has established a clearer policy framework for mining, including in environmentally sensitive areas, to foster responsible resource extraction. This move aims to provide certainty for investors and ensure communities benefit from mineral wealth through value addition, moving beyond basic corporate social responsibility handouts. The government emphasizes that mining in these areas will only proceed under stringent conditions, including independent environmental impact assessments, continuous monitoring, and adherence to international ethical standards.

The new approach is exemplified by the potential for in-situ leach (ISL) mining at Leonardville in the Omaheke Region, a proven method for uranium extraction with a minimal surface footprint. Unlike conventional mining, ISL circulates a leaching solution through wells to dissolve uranium, processing it in a closed-loop system with little landscape disturbance. This method preserves the land for other uses, such as agriculture, and offers a unique opportunity to gather scientific data under operational conditions.

Existing uranium operations in the Erongo Region have demonstrated that resource extraction and environmental protection can coexist under rigorous oversight, contributing significantly to the national economy through GDP, jobs, and foreign exchange. Extending this model to new frontiers, including ecologically sensitive zones, allows for broader community benefit from subsurface resources. The policy aims to remove investment uncertainty and ensure that economic gains are realized responsibly.

na.headline: Kapps Hotel Revival Promises Lüderitz Tourism Growth
na.dek: The historic Kapps Hotel in Lüderitz is set to reopen in early 2027 as Kapps a Kubata Loft Hotel after extensive redevelopment.
paragraphs: The Kapps Hotel, a landmark in Lüderitz since 1907, is undergoing a significant redevelopment and is slated to reopen in the first quarter of 2027 as the Kapps a Kubata Loft Hotel. The project aims to blend the building's historic character, preserving its façade, archways, and name, with modern facilities by adding two executive floors. This revival coincides with a surge in economic activity in Lüderitz, driven by offshore oil and gas exploration, increased port operations, and a rise in tourism, leading to greater demand for quality accommodation.

Nokubiko Investment (Pty) Ltd, the developer, is actively engaging with government officials, including the Minister of Environment, Tourism and Forestry, Indileni Daniel, and //Kharas governor Dawid Gertze. Minister Daniel has lauded the project as a welcome investment that aligns with Namibia’s tourism master plan by enhancing luxury offerings, preserving heritage, and expanding conference capacity in the region.

The redevelopment is expected to stimulate Lüderitz's local economy by creating jobs during construction and permanently upon opening, spanning roles in hospitality, administration, and maintenance. The project will also benefit local businesses through procurement and create opportunities for transport operators and tour guides. Furthermore, developers plan to establish off-take agreements with farmers in southern Namibia for fresh produce, opening a new market for local agricultural producers.
