ls.headline: Econet, GEM Institute Plant 500 Fruit Trees at Lesotho Schools
ls.dek: The 2026 ACT 4 Climate Change Fruit-Up School Drive aims to foster environmental education and practical climate action among over 3,000 learners.
paragraphs: Telecommunications giant Econet Telecom Lesotho, in partnership with GEM Institute and UNESCO, has launched the 2026 ACT 4 Climate Change Fruit-Up School Drive. Over 500 fruit trees will be planted at 14 schools across six districts, continuing a five-year collaboration focused on practical climate action for young Basotho. The initiative uses schools as platforms for environmental education, climate action, and skills development, with learners directly participating in tree planting and care.

Econet's Public Relations Specialist, Retšelisitsoe Nkhahle, stated that the company's commitment extends beyond connectivity, emphasizing a responsibility to contribute meaningfully to the communities served and Lesotho's future. The Fruit-Up program moves climate change education from theory to practice, enabling learners to engage in environmental conservation and fostering greener school environments. Since 2021, Econet and GEM Institute have planted 3,397 fruit trees at 54 schools, involving over 3,000 learners.

GEM Institute's Tšepang Khau highlighted the program's role in educating youth and building environmental and entrepreneurial skills, encouraging recognition of indigenous plants' potential for health and economic opportunities. UNESCO representative Mankopane Nkhono reaffirmed support for these initiatives, noting their success in developing environmental awareness and encouraging active participation in addressing climate change. The 2026 drive emphasizes climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and practical skills.

ls.headline: ABC leaders fight, party implodes
ls.dek: Party leader Kabi accuses deputy and SG of insubordination, deepening internal crisis.
paragraphs: The All Basotho Convention (ABC) party is experiencing a severe internal crisis as leader Nkaku Kabi accused his deputy, Samonyane Ntsekele, and Secretary General Thebe Mokoatle of "deliberately destabilising" the party. Kabi issued a circular detailing these accusations following an incident where Mokoatle was reportedly attacked by Kabi's bodyguards at a National Executive Committee meeting.

The once-dominant ABC, founded in 2006, has seen a significant decline since its landslide victory in the 2017 general election, where it secured 51 constituency seats. In the October 2022 polls, the party lost all its constituency seats, subsisting on only eight Proportional Representation seats. Kabi took over leadership in February 2022 from founding leader Tom Thabane.

This latest leadership dispute adds to the party's ongoing struggles with internal factionalism, which Kabi has stated he is attempting to address through a "revitalisation" strategy. The ABC previously held power in coalition governments formed after the 2012 and 2017 general elections but has since faced electoral setbacks and leadership changes.

ls.headline: Government launches M78 million solar-hybrid power project in Semonkong
ls.dek: A new solar-hybrid power project aims to provide reliable electricity to 100 families in Semonkong, addressing years of erratic power supply.
paragraphs: Semonkong residents will benefit from a M78 million government-backed solar-hybrid power project launched by Prime Minister Sam Matekane. The initiative addresses the town's long-standing issue of unreliable electricity, which has frequently been cut off overnight and at times for days, impacting businesses and essential services. The project integrates a refurbished mini-hydropower plant with solar generation, battery storage, and a diesel generator for backup, promising a more stable power supply.

The upgrade is expected to connect approximately 100 households in and around Semonkong to a consistent electricity supply. Prime Minister Matekane stated that the project aligns with the government's goal of achieving universal electricity access by 2030, reducing the nation's dependence on imported power. The World Bank is a partner in this project, aiming to improve livelihoods and build community resilience.

Local leaders highlighted the critical timing of the intervention, noting that unreliable electricity has significantly hampered economic activity in Semonkong, with past blackouts forcing businesses to close. The project involves refurbishing the town's 1990-built 220-kilowatt hydropower station, which had deteriorated and could no longer meet demand, and supplementing it with modern renewable energy solutions.

ls.headline: Rights Group Sues Judiciary Over Combined Sheriff Powers
ls.dek: Section 2 argues the current system merges Registrar, Sheriff, and Deputy Sheriff roles, threatening judicial independence and public trust.
paragraphs: Human rights organization Section 2 has filed a Constitutional Court challenge against Lesotho's Judiciary and other state bodies. The group seeks to end a "three-in-one" system that consolidates the powers of the Registrar, Sheriff, and Deputy Sheriff within the Judiciary. Section 2 president Kananelo Boloetse claims this arrangement violates the separation of powers, compromises judicial independence, and erodes public confidence in the justice system.

The lawsuit names the Judiciary, Chief Justice Sakoane Sakoane, the Registrar of the High Court and Court of Appeal, the Minister of Law and Justice, Parliament, the Law Society, the Judicial Officers Association, Sheriffs and Deputy Sheriffs, the police, and the Attorney General as respondents. Boloetse's affidavit asserts that the current legal framework improperly places executive functions within the Judiciary, creating a conflict of duties and potentially exposing vulnerable individuals to rights violations during evictions or property seizures.

At the core of the challenge are the definitions and functions of the Registrar under the Administration of Justice Act of 2011 and High Court Civil Litigation Rules of 2024. Boloetse argues that while the Registrar is defined as a judicial officer and chief administrator of the courts, the same office also acts as the Sheriff. This dual role, he contends, burdens the courts with non-judicial executive work and risks undermining their dignity and effectiveness.
